company.description: Employer named in the Jobicy listing. Check the original listing for employer details.

jobs.description:
GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.

Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit!

About this role

GiveDirectly is looking for an experienced investigator who can establish a function, not just run cases. Concerns and allegations reach us from every program and every country we work in. Each one needs to be triaged and assessed objectively, and to end in appropriate findings and recommendations.

You will manage the newly created Central Intake and Investigations Hub. It is a standalone, independent function that works across the whole organisation. The Hub investigates a range of investigations itself, and supports colleagues elsewhere who handle the rest. You will lead the team and take the most complex investigations yourself.

The bigger initial task is to establish the Hub across the organisation. How it works has been designed and agreed. What it does not yet have is standing. People need to know it exists, bring things to it early, and trust what it concludes. This matters now because GiveDirectly is growing fast. Delivery volume and headcount are both rising, and the way staff concerns are handled needs to grow with them.

Reports to: Director of Safeguarding and Investigations

Manages: Future roles including a Program Manager, Investigations and Program Manager, Intake and Reporting to be recruited once the Senior Manager role has been filled. 

Level: Senior Manager 

Location: Remote, with a requirement to overlap with an East Africa timezone by at least 3 hours, and meaningful overlap with US Eastern hours. We can only employ people in certain places at the moment, so it's worth checking our current list of eligible countries to see if yours is included. If you're based elsewhere, it's not an automatic no, but do flag it early with your recruiter. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas in the U.S. or U.K. at this time.

Travel: Occasional. Team meetings and co-locations, plus travel to a country of operation where an investigation requires it. This is not frequent, but it is not predictable either.

What you'll do

Establish a Central Intake and Investigations Hub across the organisation: Take an agreed design and make it something people use. Build the relationships with the People team, Internal Audit, Safeguarding, HR Managers and Country Directors to ensure concerns are managed effectively. Refine how intake, triage and allocation work in practice as you learn what holds up.

Lead the most complex investigations yourself. Establish the facts, produce the findings report and make recommendations.

Set the investigation standard and hold other people to it: Define what a good investigation looks like at GiveDirectly. Provide oversight and support where Internal Audit or Safeguarding lead a staff related matter, and quality assure what comes out of it. Decide what training the organisation needs and set its direction.

Own the record and what it tells the organisation: Create and hold the system of record for staff matters. Make sure findings and documentation are captured centrally, whoever led the case. Run regular reporting and calibration with the People team, Internal Audit, Safeguarding, Country Directors and ExCo. Sign off on relevant internal and external reporting. 

Make the function work at scale through the responsible use of technology and data: Shape the design of the case management system and its controls, so that staff investigation records sit only where they should. Find the practical places where automation and AI reduce manual work in triage, documentation and reporting. Build the hub so that growth in concern volume does not simply mean a bigger team.

Set up and lead the team: Recruit for, manage and develop a Program Manager, Investigations and the Program Manager, Intake and Reporting. Set their priorities, review their work and build their capability.

What success looks like in 12 to 18 months

Concerns reach the hub as a matter of course, from every country and function.

People come to the hub early and while a matter is still manageable, because they have found it useful rather than because they were told to.

Investigations are handled consistently, whoever leads them, and findings reports hold up when they are challenged.

The hub is understood across the organisation as an independent central resource.

Internal and External reporting tells its audience something they did not already know about patterns, themes and where risk is concentrating.

The People team, Internal Audit, Safeguarding and country leadership treat the hub as a resource they rely on rather than a process they comply with.

Additional hires for the hub are capable, developing, and the function runs day to day without you in the room.

Why this role

You build it. This is a new function with a mandate and a set of agreed boundaries. How it actually works is largely what you make it.

Genuine independence. The hub is designed to be objective and to handle complex matters.

Breadth. You will work across every function and every country GiveDirectly operates in.

It matters. Getting this right protects staff and recipients, and protects the trust that lets GiveDirectly move a great deal of money to people who need it.

What we are looking for:

How you work matters as much as your investigation skills.

Trusted by the people you also hold to account. You can tell someone that the handling of a matter was wrong, and still have a strong working relationship with them the following week. People Managers, Internal Audit, Safeguarding and country leadership should want to call you early rather than after things have gone wrong.

You motivate and influence people who don't report to you. The Hub has no direct line management over Internal Audit, Safeguarding, the People team or country leadership, and it needs all of them to do the work well. You build the relationships and shape best practice.

Impartial, and visibly so. People may try to influence you. You will be told the answer before you have found it. You hold to process and evidence without turning it into a fight, and you record what you could not establish as carefully as what you could.

You build what isn't there yet. This function is being shaped by you. You are comfortable where the priorities are clear, but the road to them is not. You would rather design a solution rather than wait to be handed one.

You work alongside people. Some of the investigative work is done by other teams, and your expertise is what lifts its quality. You get into the detail with colleagues, you are clear about what good looks like and what still needs doing, and you see it through with them.

Steady with difficult material. You work with content of abuse and misconduct without losing sight of the people involved, and without carrying it in ways that wear you down.

On experience, we are looking for:

Exceptional alignment with GiveDirectly Values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity. 

5-7 years of experience leading workplace (misconduct) investigations, including matters involving senior staff and allegations of sexual misconduct. You have run these end to end, from terms of reference to findings report.

Experience in setting investigation standards and quality assuring other people's work, not only conducting investigations yourself.

A working understanding of employee relations and of where an investigation ends and an employment decision begins. You have worked alongside other teams without blurring the lines of responsibility.

Experience across multiple countries and legal contexts, including where local law shapes how we may investigate and how staff must be treated.

Trauma-informed and survivor-centred practice in how you plan interviews, handle disclosures and support the people involved.

Has made technology work for investigative teams. You have set up or improved investigative system, built reporting from case data, or introduced tools that changed how a team worked. You have used AI in professional work and can say where it helped, where it did not, and how you handled confidentiality.

Language Requirement: Professional fluency in English, plus professional working proficiency in one of French, Swahili or Portuguese. Investigative interviews are often confidential and conducted in these languages.

Why work at GiveDirectly?

At GiveDirectly, we work to ensure that you have everything you need to excel in your role and on your team, including:

A positive and supportive team with opportunities for advancement 

A demonstrated commitment to helping all staff develop and grow

A competitive salary, including bonus

A robust health benefits plan (exact details will vary by country)

Unlimited PTO (that we encourage staff to take!)

Read more about our ongoing diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts here and about our decision to move our central support teams to remote first here.

Compensation

At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here.

Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income.

Working at GiveDirectly

GiveDirectly is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to the person’s race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Flagging for US applicants: We invite you to "Know Your Rights" as an applicant.

Commitment to Safeguarding

As a global organization working with communities to eliminate extreme poverty, GiveDirectly takes the safeguarding of its recipients, staff, and partners seriously. jobs.description:
Posit's mission is to create free and open-source software for data science, scientific research, and technical communication to enhance the production and consumption of knowledge by everyone, regardless of economic means. We are a different kind of software company, and we’re proud to build and sell products that help people understand and improve the world through data.

About the Team

Posit’s Solutions Engineering (Sol-Eng) team aims to reduce the distance between customers of our professional products and open source offerings. 

We help our customers – especially their IT/SysAdmin teams – deploy, install, configure, and use our professional products. We aim to bring curiosity and empathy to every customer engagement, leaning into the customer experiences as they seek to get value from open source data science.

But that’s only half the job.

As we learn about what customers want and need, we use that knowledge to improve our products, documentation, and processes.

On Sol-Eng, you’ll play an essential role in both unblocking and empowering customers and making Posit and our products work better in the future.

People who thrive in this role tend to:

Find joy in working directly with and unblocking customers. This role is customer-facing. 

Love learning and sharing your knowledge of the server infrastructure and architecture that underlies enterprise data science. You’ll be an advisor to IT teams who administer Posit’s products in a wide variety of architectures and with a range of integrations. You have exposure to some of these topics and technologies (e.g. cloud services, Linux, Kubernetes, Docker, Slurm, authentication, connecting to data sources) and look forward to opportunities to dive deeply and learn in other areas. Knowing all of these topics on Day 1 is not required, but having interest in learning more about how they work is fundamental to the job.

Be curious about data science workflows and use cases. We make tools to multiply the impact of Data Scientists who work in open source. You won’t be doing data science or writing code, but you’ll need to understand what a Data Scientist does (e.g., exploratory data analysis, modeling, reporting, app development). . Prior experience specifically with data science or our professional products is not necessary, but may be helpful.

Be hungry and humble. Sol-Eng covers an impossibly broad technical scope.. Great Sol-Eng team members are quick to admit what they don’t know and constantly seek to learn more. As a trusted advisor to customers, your credibility comes from being honest about the limits of your knowledge and following through to close the gaps.

Find excitement in having many demands on your time, rather than overwhelm. The Sol-Eng team has close relationships with almost every other team at Posit. There’s no limit to the different projects Sol-Eng could take on, being able to choose important things (with help and guidance from managers) and ignore distractions is a key skill for a Posit Solutions Engineer.

What you’ll own own:

Serving as a proactive, ongoing technical advisor to customers discussing server configurations and architectures, supporting technical strategy planning, and sharing best practices for doing open source data science at scale with Posit’s professional products. You’ll collaborate with sales and customer success to enable the customer to realize the full value of their Posit environment. 

Scaling our reach through webinars, talks, workshops, documentation, automation, and how-tos that help customers adopt Posit products.

Leading scoped, project-based implementation work, from onboarding through delivery of defined outcomes.

Providing the voice of the customer to other teams at Posit, especially Product Management and Product Engineering.

What you’ll help with:

Improving our team’s processes so our workflows facilitate us doing great work, taking adequate focus time, and having time off to rest and recharge.

Setting the direction of our products by influencing the Product Management and engineering teams.

You will learn...

So much.

No one has ever (or ever will) start on Sol-Eng knowing everything we do. Strong candidates for this role generally have prior experience with approximately half of the things below.

How to navigate deeply technical post-sales customer calls and have the ability to speak about technical topics to internal and external audiences of different levels. Even people with substantial customer experience find that Sol-Eng demands new depths of empathy, curiosity, and clarity of thinking and explanation. 

How Posit’s Pro Products work. On customer calls, you will be the expert on our Pro Products – explaining how to install and configure them, as well as how they help make life better for Data Scientists.

How to speak fluently about enterprise infrastructure. Solutions Engineers help our customers IT/Admins determine the best product architecture for them, which requires they speak knowledgeably about integrations to other data (science) tools and platforms, and how to get things done on Linux servers including system administration, authentication, networking, and virtualization.

What to expect:

Within 1 month, you’ll…

Meet the rest of the Sol-Eng team and start meeting members of Customer Success, Sales, and other nearby teams.

Configure Posit’s Pro Products for yourself to start learning the ins and outs.

Have joined dozens of IT architecture and post-sales calls with IT/Admins of Posit’s Pro products.

Within 3 months, you’ll...

Lead customer calls, helping our customers determine how Posit’s Pro products fit into their existing data and technology stacks. You won’t need to know all the answers, but you will lead with curiosity to build the right mental models that will allow you to go back to find answers.

Be comfortable discussing general architectures and deployment patterns for our product

Begin getting hands on with customers who are installing and maintaining our products, looking over their shoulders and suggesting how to set up and configure their environments.

Within 12 months, you’ll…

Contribute to projects in roles of escalating size and scope.

Take on larger, more strategic, and higher-touch customer engagements that might include weekly meetings with the same customer.

Posit offers competitive compensation with extensive human-first, people-focused benefits to prioritize your personal and financial well-being. Individual pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, and skillset. This hiring range reflects base salary and assumes that the job will be performed in the United States.

Hiring Range

$141,800—$187,110 USD

Working at Posit:

We welcome all talented colleagues and are committed to a culture that represents diversity in all its forms.

We prioritize giving ourselves “focus time” to get deep work done. We minimize meetings and attempt to operate asynchronously.

We are a learning organization and take mentorship and career growth seriously. We hope to learn from you and we anticipate that you will also deepen your skills, influence, and leadership as a result of working at Posit.

We operate under a unique sustainable business model: We have over 50% of our engineering dedicated to creating free and open source software. We are profitable and we plan to be around decades from now.

Posit is a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) and a Certified B Corporation®, which means our open-source mission is codified into our charter. As a result, our corporate decisions balance the community's interests, customers, employees, and shareholders. Hear more about why we think this matters here.

Notable:

We offer competitive compensation with extensive human-first, people-focused benefits to prioritize your personal and financial well-being. These benefits apply to full-time positions only.

100% of medical, dental, and vision insurance premiums are covered for employees and their families! Fertility and gender-affirming healthcare is included in all of our plans.

Supplemental mental health and wellness benefits are available via Ginger even if you don’t opt in to our insurance plans, including Ginger for teen family members.

Posit's gender-neutral paid parental leave policy covers all new parents, including foster and adoptive parents.

All full-time employees are eligible for 401k enrollment starting on day one.

After six months of employment, Posit provides a substantial yearly match to employee 401K contributions.

An annual profit-sharing bonus for employees recognizes our team’s contributions to company performance across the year.

We are a 100% distributed team. You are also welcome to come into our Boston office. 

We offer a $400 monthly reimbursement for coworking space rental if you prefer to work away from home. 

Our Lifestyle Savings Account offers an initial deposit of $1800 and then an additional quarterly stipend of $375 to cover the costs of professional development, wellness, financial health, charitable giving, and remote work support.

We provide a flexible environment with a generous vacation policy that encourages a minimum of four weeks PTO per year plus 15 paid company holidays.

Are you excited about this role but not sure if your experience aligns with every qualification in the job description? That’s okay. We know multiple perspectives are essential for a thriving organization and we'd still love to hear from you! 

Posit is committed to being a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage applicants of different backgrounds, cultures, genders, experiences, abilities, and perspectives to apply. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, age, physical disability, or length of time spent unemployed.

GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.

You will mentor and develop Delivery Managers and surge roster members, contribute to the strategic direction of the team, and serve in assigned functional roles during responses. Flex enables our users to pay rent throughout the month on a schedule that better fits their finances and budget. Our mission is to empower as many renters as possible with flexibility over their most significant recurring expense. After deliberately keeping a stealth profile as we built up unprecedented investor support and an enthusiastic user base, we are looking for motivated individuals to help us keep our mission growing. Will you be a part of the team?

About Our Opportunity

Flex exists to make paying rent work the way real life actually works — smoothing out cash flow, helping renters avoid late fees, and letting them build credit instead of falling behind. As a Senior Staff Software Engineer, you'll oversee the technical roadmap for the team, working across APIs, SDKs, and Web experiences. Who thrives here?

jobs.description:
Who is Boulevard? 

Boulevard provides the first and only client experience platform for appointment-based, self-care businesses. We empower our customers to give their clients more of the magical moments that matter most.

Before launching in 2016, our founders spent months interviewing salon managers and working behind front desks to understand their pain points so we could design a modern, user-friendly platform that meets the unique needs of their business. Our roots may be in hair salons, but we are built for the broader self-care industry, including many types of salons, spas, medspa, barbershops, and more. Our technology not only helps our customers survive but thrive. Take a look at how we (and YOU) can make that happen. 

We have an insatiable curiosity and embrace experimentation. We believe that simple solutions require the most sophistication, and we design each and every detail to maximize potential, power, and impact. Do our values match? Read through our story and what we value the most.

Our team values and celebrates our diverse backgrounds. Being open about who we are and what we do allows us to do the best work of our lives. We believe in equal opportunity for all, and you should too.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Customer Experience team is responsible for launching, supporting, and strengthening relationships with Boulevard's customers. As the Onboarding Manager for our Small/Medium Business segment, you will lead a team of 8–12 Onboarding Specialists (OSs) responsible for driving fast, consistent, and high-quality activations across our highest-volume customer segment.

This role is ideal for a leader who thrives on operational rigor, forecasting discipline, and coaching a team to hit velocity targets at scale. SMB success is defined by speed, standardization, and repeatability — helping customers reach value quickly through a consistent, well-executed process. You'll be accountable for outcomes, not activity: activation velocity, forecast accuracy, and team execution quality. Above all, you'll ensure every customer is positioned to achieve long-term success by balancing implementation speed with solution quality, customer readiness, and adoption.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Team Leadership & Development

Manage and develop a team of 8–12 OSs through structured 1:1s, Gong-based coaching, and performance reviews.

Drive a culture of ownership and accountability — coaching specialists to lead customer timelines firmly rather than passively tracking status.

Run structured weekly portfolio reviews covering On Track, At Risk, On Hold/Delayed, Forecasted Out, and Aging accounts, with a defined recovery plan and owner for every at-risk account.

Own new hire ramp quality, volume, and velocity, including acting as a buddy/shadow resource for new specialists' early customer assignments.

Develop future leaders through mentoring, stretch assignments, succession planning, and career development conversations.

Execution & Portfolio Management

Own team activation velocity against benchmark targets.

Track and enforce efficiency standards across the funnel to eliminate backlog drag.

Maintain forecast accuracy and hold specialists accountable for defensible, evidence-based commits.

Analyze operational trends to identify root causes impacting activation velocity, forecast accuracy, cancellations, customer delays, and portfolio health.

Ensure customers consistently complete implementation milestones and activation readiness standards.

Customer Risk Leadership

Own customer risk identification, mitigation strategies, and executive escalations to maximize activation success.

Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement

Identify systemic bottlenecks across onboarding and recommend scalable process improvements.

Use portfolio trends and operational data to influence tooling, playbooks, customer journey improvements, and cross-functional initiatives.

Partner with Operations to improve reporting, automation, and onboarding efficiency.

Coaching & Quality

Score and review Gong calls per the coaching cadence.

Deliver documented coaching tied to specific behaviors: driving vs. tracking, handling pushback, timeline control, and escalation discipline.

Run team meetings that are portfolio-focused and action-oriented — activation pacing, risk cohort review, backlog recovery, and skill development.

Cross-Functional Business Partnership

Partner with Sales and Customer Success to ensure clean pre-sale to post-sale handoffs for the SMB segment.

Serve as the voice of the SMB customer across Product and Engineering, surfacing friction points from high-volume onboarding patterns.

Partner with Revenue Operations and Finance on capacity planning, reporting integrity, and operational efficiency.

Identify and champion automation, tooling, and process efficiencies that increase throughput without sacrificing quality.

Maintain data hygiene standards across project management and implementation platforms.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

3+ years in SaaS onboarding, implementation, or customer success, with at least 1–2 years leading a team.

Demonstrated ability to manage a high-volume portfolio with velocity and forecasting discipline.

Strong coaching skills — able to translate call reviews and metrics into specific, actionable behavior change.

Comfort operating in a fast-paced, metrics-driven environment where speed and consistency matter.

Experience with data hygiene and reporting integrity in CRM tools (Salesforce or similar).

Experience with project management or implementation platforms.

Ability to hold a team accountable to standards while maintaining a supportive, development-oriented culture.

Strong written and verbal communication skills for both customer-facing escalations and internal reporting.

BONUS POINTS FOR

Experience managing high-volume onboarding motions.

Experience with Gong or similar conversation intelligence tools for coaching at scale.

Experience within wellness, healthcare, med spa, salon, or service-based industries.

Familiarity with GuideCX or related SaaS operational platforms.

Six Sigma, PMP, or other process-improvement credentials.

SUCCESS IN THIS ROLE

In Your First 30 Days

Gain a deep understanding of Boulevard's SMB onboarding methodology, tools, and team structure.

Complete 1:1s with all direct reports and begin baseline Gong call reviews.

Build cross-functional relationships across Sales, Support, Product, and Customer Success.

By 90 Days

Independently run the weekly portfolio governance cadence with clear ownership on all at-risk/aging accounts.

Demonstrate improving forecast accuracy and activation pacing against targets.

Establish a consistent coaching rhythm and begin closing identified skill gaps.

By 6 Months and Beyond

Consistently hit or exceed activation velocity, forecast accuracy, and CSAT benchmarks.

Reduce aging backlog and eliminate systemic bottlenecks within your portfolio.

Be recognized as a driver of team performance improvement and a trusted escalation point for the SMB segment.

KEY PERFORMANCE METRICS

Activation velocity

Forecast accuracy

CSAT

Cancellation rate

Portfolio health

Customer readiness / milestone completion

Time to Value

Time to First Appointment / Working Session

Ramp time for new hires

Coaching effectiveness

Risk recovery rate

Team engagement

KEY ATTRIBUTES FOR SUCCESS

Execution-oriented with strong operational discipline

Comfortable holding a team accountable to firm standards and timelines

Data-driven — treats forecasting and portfolio health as core to the job, not overhead

Strong coach who ties feedback to specific, observable behaviors

Thrives on speed, consistency, and process adherence at scale

Proactive communicator who escalates early rather than waiting for problems to surface

How we take care of our team

Our business is deeply immersed in an industry that’s centered around helping people feel their best, so we know that taking care of yourself isn’t selfish; it’s essential. That’s why our culture pairs high standards with genuine care. We don't glorify burnout or wear ‘always on’ as a badge of honor. Instead, we’ve created benefits designed to support you inside and outside of work, so you can bring your best self to both.

Here’s how we support you:

Competitive base pay and performance bonus eligibility because you deserve to be rewarded for your impact.

Equity participation for all full-time employees because we believe the people helping build Boulevard should share in our long-term success.

Comprehensive medical coverage with up to 100% employee premium coverage and 75% dependent coverage to help take care of you and your loved ones.

An annual $1,200 HSA employer contribution for eligible plans to help support healthcare costs and future planning.

100% covered dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, ensuring you stay healthy, protected, and ready for whatever life brings.

12 weeks of fully paid U.S. parental leave supporting all new parents equally as they take the time to bond, adjust, and be present when welcoming a new family member.

Flexible paid time off, plus 10 U.S. company holidays, where you are encouraged to rest, recharge, and take the time you need, guilt-free. 

Fully remote with support, including a $200 home office setup allowance and a $50 monthly WFH reimbursement so your workspace is set up for success. 

$200 quarterly Boulevard Bucks to prioritize your well-being and stay connected to the industry we serve.

And other perks like One Medical membership and Employee Assistant Program.

We are seeking a skilled Senior Software Engineer to join our engineering team. In this role, you will bring a builder’s instinct to a team working at the intersection of data science, infrastructure, and AI. You will help us build new capabilities and features in our product suite, including things we haven’t yet imagined possible, and you will drive those changes forward into our customers’ hands.

About you

You are an enthusiastic generalist who thrives in the face of ambiguous requirements—an engineer who is just as good at starting things as you are at finishing them. Some qualities we value most:

High agency

You are driven. When something important feels daunting or underspecified, your first instinct is to prototype to clarify the value you can deliver, rather than wait for someone to give you the answers.

Boldness in learning

You are genuinely unafraid to tackle unfamiliar subjects. You know that nobody is an expert in everything, and you don't let unfamiliarity be a reason for not trying. You're not afraid to ask questions and make mistakes, because learning new techniques feels like an adventure and we share what we learn as a team. Proficiency in either Go or Typescript as well as in either Python or R, and experience with backend systems, data tooling, and data science frameworks are helpful for this role. Eagerness and boldness to learn is essential. 

User empathy and product sense

You make judgment calls on behalf of users with minimal up front guidance and are willing to be wrong, because you will learn. Prior domain expertise with data science as a practice may help, but it is not the only way. Regardless, you lead with empathy: you optimize for solving a real customer problem, not for technical purity.

Collaborative curiosity

You are generous. When you learn something useful, your first instinct is to share it. You teach as readily as you learn, ask questions without ego, admit what you don't know, and lend a hand when someone's stuck.

Interest in AI

You are interested not just in using AI in your work, but building tools for customers to use AI in their own work. You also are curious, and you question when AI is not the right answer for a particular problem. You lean on your user empathy when building: knowing that some of our customers use and love AI in data science and others don’t or are restricted from using it.

Results-driven

You are focused on delivering measurable value to customers. You have a strong technical background with a track record of shipping successful products.

Ship code changes that meaningfully improves the experience for our customers.

Within one month, you will…

See your changes reflected in our public releases.

Participate in feature planning and provide feedback.

Within three months, you will…

Plan features and drive their development.

Have a track record of teaching team members; both from your expertise and things you learn as you build. 

Have a track record of learning: both from the things you learned and taught us along the way; and from listening to internal users, external users, and how our customers use our products.

Within six months, you will…

Point to new features you built that we hadn’t even dreamed were possible.

Who is Boulevard? 

Boulevard provides the first and only client experience platform for appointment-based, self-care businesses. We empower our customers to give their clients more of the magical moments that matter most.

Before launching in 2016, our founders spent months interviewing salon managers and working behind front desks to understand their pain points so we could design a modern, user-friendly platform that meets the unique needs of their business. Our roots may be in hair salons, but we are built for the broader self-care industry, including many types of salons, spas, medspa, barbershops, and more. Our technology not only helps our customers survive but thrive. Take a look at how we (and YOU) can make that happen. 

We have an insatiable curiosity and embrace experimentation. We believe that simple solutions require the most sophistication, and we design each and every detail to maximize potential, power, and impact. Do our values match? Read through our story and what we value the most.

Our team values and celebrates our diverse backgrounds. Being open about who we are and what we do allows us to do the best work of our lives. We believe in equal opportunity for all, and you should too.

Come do the best work of your life at Boulevard.

As a Mid-Market Customer Success Manager, you'll own a book of sophisticated, multi-location self-care businesses from start to finish. Retention is your top priority, and you'll drive renewals and expansion with sound judgment on account health, risk, and escalation. You'll help the salons, spas, and medspas we serve get lasting value from Boulevard, and you'll do it for an industry we cherish.

You'll partner closely with Onboarding, Sales, Support, and Product, and you'll work remotely. We're large enough to transform the industry and small enough that you'll see the impact of your work every day.

What you'll do:

Own the customer relationship after onboarding, guiding customers toward lasting value and long-term success with Boulevard.

Own retention by watching account health and risk signals and leading contract renewals with data-driven judgment.

Run structured check-ins, business reviews, and account planning for your Mid-Market book of business.

Build and maintain trusted relationships with stakeholders across each account.

Advocate for customers by sharing feedback, trends, and risks with our product and cross-functional teams.

Spot opportunities to boost product adoption and drive upsell and cross-sell within your book.

Be a go-to resource for newer CSMs on complex account situations and escalations.

What you'll need to thrive:

3+ years managing a Mid-Market book of business, with proven success in retention, renewals, and relationship management.

Strong business acumen: you understand customer goals, spot risk early, and know when to escalate and bring in internal partners.

A growth mindset: you use customer context and usage data to make clear, data-driven recommendations and spot expansion opportunities.

Who We Are

We are solving real-world problems leveraging robotics, machine learning and computer vision, among other disciplines, with a mindful eye towards the end-to-end user experience. JOB OVERVIEW

The Financial Analyst is responsible for supporting financial planning, analysis, and decision-making processes, with a focus on budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, and scenario modeling.

JOB DUTIES

Lead the preparation, analysis, and maintenance of detailed financial models and forecasts to inform business decisions.

Leverage advanced Excel/Google Sheets and ChatGPT to automate and simplify complex reporting processes, ensuring higher efficiency and accuracy.

Act as a trusted financial partner to business units, collaborating with cross-functional teams to understand their financial needs and deliver actionable insights.

Apply solid knowledge of accounting principles to ensure the integrity of financial reporting and assist in closing processes.

Proficiency in advanced Google Sheets and Excel, with the ability to create and manipulate complex financial models.

Strong knowledge of budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, and financial reporting.

"Comfort using emerging productivity tools (e.g., ChatGPT, scripting, workflow automation) to enhance efficiency."

Strong business acumen, with the ability to communicate financial information effectively to non-financial stakeholders.

Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and communication skills.

jobs.description:
Client Director

About This Role

As a Client Director at Nash, you will help transform how the largest enterprises reimagine how they manage last-mile delivery. This is a strategic, high-impact role focused on closing complex, high-value deals and shaping how our most important customers adopt Nash’s AI-powered logistics infrastructure.

You will play a crucial role on our Go-To-Market (GTM) team in scaling Nash’s enterprise sales motion, building predictable revenue streams with aggressive quotas. Your focus will be on industries where Nash has already established strong traction: Grocery, Retail, Convenience, Food, and Pharmaceuticals. You will leverage our technical edge, agility, and grit to drive further success in these markets.

Your passion and expertise will help us build the Nash brand and further accelerate our rapid expansion. This is a full-cycle role with support from marketing, product, and data, and your work will help customers evolve from fragmented delivery workflows to unified, intelligent logistics infrastructure.

Opportunities is the West, Midwest and Northeast Regions

Key Responsibilities

Build and manage a complex sales pipeline from scratch, focusing on high-value, enterprise-level deals. This includes identifying, prospecting, demoing, negotiating, and closing deals with a strategic approach.

Develop and execute a high-touch playbook for each target account that leverages a strong outbound motion, strategic networking, and targeted messaging to engage and convert key named accounts.

Establish and grow Executive - Level relationships within strategic, named accounts across the grocery, convenience, pharmaceutical, and retail industries, positioning Nash as a trusted partner in their delivery operations.

Collaborate closely with product, marketing, and engineering teams to align Nash’s offerings with customer needs. Provide actionable feedback that refines sales strategies and supports product development.

Maintain a deep understanding of target markets and customer pain points. Contribute to internal feedback loops that drive product development and marketing strategies, keeping Nash ahead of market demands.

Routinely update CRM and other sales tools with accurate activity data, deal progressions, revenue projections and next steps, maintaining transparency and strong sales hygiene.

Requirements

5+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role

Proven track record of consistent quota over-achievement in complex accounts and $1M+ ARR transactions

Experience handling and owning enterprise deal sizes and C-Level relationships

Willing and comfortable with strategic outbound prospecting

A self-starter with a high level of motivation who sees themselves as a major stakeholder in Nash's growth. Demonstrated ability to manage responsibilities independently while contributing to team success.

Strong curiosity in understanding customer needs and challenges, with the ability to ask insightful questions that uncover deeper issues and craft tailored solutions.

Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to convey complex ideas and technical concepts clearly to stakeholders at all levels, from C-suite executives to technical teams. Capable of presenting Nash’s value proposition persuasively and handling objections effectively.

More about Nash

Nash is the platform that powers modern logistics.

Commerce has inverted. For decades, customers came to where products and services were. Now products and services come to them, on their terms, in real time. That shift has turned every company into a logistics company, even though almost none of them were built to be one. Couriers, fleets, gig workers, parcel carriers, in-store labor, and increasingly autonomous systems all have to be coordinated in real time, against tighter windows and rising expectations, with hard-fought customer trust on the line.

Nash unifies decisioning, execution, and capacity into a single programmable platform. Real-time, AI-native intelligence determines what should happen, operational control executes it, and the platform dynamically orchestrates capacity from any source: a company's own fleets, partners, or the Nash delivery network. Whether a job involves a courier, a gig driver, an internal fleet, a store employee, a technician, or an autonomous vehicle, Nash selects the right resource and manages execution through completion.

We power delivery and logistics for some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, 7-Eleven, and Woolworths, alongside platforms like Shopify and Toast. Over the next decade, logistics will become as foundational to commerce as payments, cloud, and connectivity. Nash is the platform that powers it.

jobs.description:
Background

Nash powers the logistics infrastructure behind some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, and 7-Eleven, along with platforms like Shopify and Toast. We are scaling fast, the category is forming around us, and we are building the product marketing function from scratch. We're hiring our first Product Marketing Lead to own positioning, narrative, launches, and the strategic voice of the platform that is becoming foundational to modern commerce.

The Role

This is the strategic seat where positioning, narrative, customer truth, competitive worldview, and launch craft come together. It is also where the next chapter of Nash's product strategy is shaped. Product marketing can take many different forms in different organizations... It can be a function to spit out whitepapers and datasheets, a megaphone for product management, or… it can be something very different: a force multiplier for the whole organization. We're looking for the latter. 

You'll report directly to our Chief Growth Officer (whose career has been building and leading marketing, growth, and product organizations at companies like Twilio, Plaid, and Salesforce). You'll work as a peer to our Product Team, and alongside our CEO, our CTO, and a small, senior, fast-moving cross-functional group across product, engineering, sales, and growth. The bar for taste, craft, and strategic thinking on this team is high, and the trajectory for someone strong in this seat is significant.

How We Think About PMM

The best PMMs sit at the intersection of three rare skills: technical curiosity, business acumen, and creativity.

You don't need to be a coder, but you need to understand technical implementation, tradeoffs, and be able to talk to a technical audience credibly enough to know what they'll ask next.

You don't need to be a salesperson, but you need to read buying behavior, understand the worldview of the decision-maker, and articulate the value of the problem we're resolving (not the value of our product). You talk in the language of the customer, not the language of our company.

You don't need to be a designer or a copywriter, but you need to write narratives with emotional resonance, position with clear differentiation, and find the experiment, the data, or the execution model that actually moves the needle.

The skills are hard enough to find in one person. The harder bar is what you do with them. Great PMM teams are not measured on what they did. They are measured on what they got the company to achieve together. They don't ask the org to enable them. They enable the org. They earn strategic influence by inspiring the company with a common vision, and then get the whole company pulling together in the same direction.

How We Work: AI-Native, By Default

Product marketing at Nash is AI-native and builder-led. We're looking for a PMM who has fundamentally rewired their workflow around AI, not someone who occasionally uses ChatGPT to clean up an email. Someone who reaches for Claude, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Replit, and whatever ships next week as instinctively as they reach for a Google doc.

The reason is straightforward: the speed and surface area of what one product marketer can produce has changed by an order of magnitude in the last eighteen months. Customer interview synthesis, competitive teardowns, narrative iteration, message testing at scale, launch asset production, sales enablement, internal narrative documents: every loop has compressed. We want someone who feels that in their bones and uses it to compound their craft, not replace it.

We still deeply value the soul, the originality, the conviction, and the taste that can only come from a real product marketer who has actually sat with hundreds of customers and built a worldview. But we need to pair that with the velocity AI brings, so insight reaches the org and the market while it still matters.

In practice this looks like having Claude synthesize forty customer calls into the real patterns (and dampening the lone noisy ones) before you write the narrative, running ten message variants against synthetic personas before you brief the real ones, prototyping a launch landing page in Replit on the same day you finalize the positioning, building a competitive intel system that updates itself, and treating prompt craft, model choice, and tool-chaining as part of your PMM practice.

If your reaction to a new AI tool is curiosity and a Saturday afternoon experiment, you'll fit here. If you believe AI will never replace , you probably won't.

What You'll Do

- Own Nash's positioning and narrative across audiences: enterprise retailers, grocers, pharmacies, restaurants, healthcare, platforms, partners, and the broader category we're shaping

- Lead launches end to end, from shaping what gets built and when, through messaging, assets, sales enablement, and post-launch measurement of whether the launch actually moved the business

- Be the most authoritative voice on the customer inside Nash. Distill the full breadth of customer signal into the patterns that matter, so Product can build against truth and Sales can sell against reality

- Own competitive intelligence: a living worldview on every competitor that matters, refreshed continuously, that a Sales rep can use in a deal at 4pm on a Friday

- Build the launch system itself (the cadence, the rituals, the templates, the prompts, the playbooks) so each launch compounds rather than getting reinvented

- Partner with Sales as a strategic peer. Be the deepest student of our market, our buyers, and the problems they're actually trying to solve, and the best teacher of it across the org. But also build the system so your knowledge scales without you: living competitive intel, talk tracks grounded in real customer signal, enablement that a rep can pull from at 4pm on a Friday without pinging anyone. The best PMM isn't the one who answers every ping. It's the one who built the system that made most of them unnecessary.

- Partner with Product as a peer. Challenge the roadmap with customer signal, shape what we build, not just how we describe it

- Equip the org. Pricing, packaging, deal desk, content, web, sales plays: make Nash collectively faster and sharper at every customer touchpoint

- Build and grow the PMM function over time as Nash scales

Requirements

- 8+ years in product marketing or adjacent roles, with shipped work at a high-growth B2B technology company that you can defend in detail (the decisions, the tradeoffs, the outcomes)

- Demonstrated ability to operate at the intersection of technical, business, and creative, not just one of the three

- Has owned positioning and launches for a complex platform product (infrastructure, fintech, devtools, data, logistics) where the buyer is technical and the stakes are real

- Active, daily use of Claude (or equivalent LLM) and AI prototyping tools like Replit as the core of your workflow of how you actually get things done, not just a copy editing tool.

- Strong narrative and writing craft. You can hold a worldview in your head and turn it into copy that sticks

- Comfortable in the data. Funnel, deal, pipeline, win/loss; happy to sit in a CRM and pull the truth yourself rather than wait for a dashboard

- Customer-obsessed. You measure your week by how many real customer conversations you had, not how many decks you produced

- Strong opinions, communicated clearly, updated quickly when the evidence changes

- Has built or scaled a PMM function before, or is genuinely ready to do so for the first time

- Bonus: prior experience in logistics, commerce infrastructure, or B2B platforms with a technical buyer; time spent as a PM or in a customer-facing role earlier in your career; built and shipped your own side project using AI tools

- Location: Hybrid remote/in-office, Bay Area preferred, Fully remote considered for right candidate.

How to Apply

Send us your resume, a portfolio or links to launches and positioning work you've owned, and a short note on the launch or narrative you're most proud of and why. If you'd rather skip the cover letter and send a Loom walking us through a piece of work, or a Replit prototype of the Nash homepage you'd build instead of ours, that is very much encouraged.

Want to grab our attention and bypass the Recruiting platform? Record a video introducing yourself at testimonials.nash.ai with code JOIN-NASH - you'll get the benefit of your application instantly notifying us via Slack, and we'll get some much needed testing coverage on our latest PMM-focused claude build:)

More about Nash

Nash is the platform that powers modern logistics.

Commerce has inverted. For decades, customers came to where products and services were. Now products and services come to them, on their terms, in real time. That shift has turned every company into a logistics company, even though almost none of them were built to be one. Couriers, fleets, gig workers, parcel carriers, in-store labor, and increasingly autonomous systems all have to be coordinated in real time, against tighter windows and rising expectations, with hard-fought customer trust on the line.

Nash unifies decisioning, execution, and capacity into a single programmable platform. Real-time, AI-native intelligence determines what should happen, operational control executes it, and the platform dynamically orchestrates capacity from any source: a company's own fleets, partners, or the Nash delivery network. Whether a job involves a courier, a gig driver, an internal fleet, a store employee, a technician, or an autonomous vehicle, Nash selects the right resource and manages execution through completion.

We power delivery and logistics for some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, 7-Eleven, and Woolworths, alongside platforms like Shopify and Toast. Over the next decade, logistics will become as foundational to commerce as payments, cloud, and connectivity. Nash is the platform that powers it.

Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman (2x Founder, MIT) and Aziz Alghunaim (2x Founder, 2x YC, Ex-Palantir, MIT) and is backed by Y Combinator, a16z, and other top investors. We are headquartered in San Francisco.

What You’ll Love About Us

✅ Competitive compensation and opportunity for equity
✅ Flexible paid time off

jobs.description:
Not all heroes wear capes — but plenty of them use toilet paper

Want to challenge yourself at a purpose-led scale up AND make a difference in the world? Come join the revolootion!

Funny name, serious business

We make eco-friendly products and donate 50% of our profits to provide clean water and help build toilets for the billions of people who lack proper access. So far, we’ve contributed over $18 million AUD (roughly $12.5 million USD) to fund sanitation projects around the globe. Basically, we’re really good at doing good. 

With hubs in Australia, the Philippines, China, the US, UK and Europe, our amazing team of 200+ work to make the biggest possible impact for people and the planet. Over the next couple of years, we’re hoping to increase our annual donation tenfold to get us closer to our dream of everyone in the world having access to clean water and sanitation services.

A bit about the role

As our Senior Legal Counsel, you’ll be instrumental in supporting Who Gives A Crap’s growth and impact. You’ll take the lead on complex commercial matters, including significant contracts and high-stakes negotiations. Beyond that, you’ll provide expert guidance across global legal areas like intellectual property, regulatory compliance (in close collaboration with our Privacy & Compliance Specialist), and corporate governance. You’ll also serve as a crucial point of contact for day to day legal inquiries and play a key role in educating the business on legal best practices. Working closely with the Head of Legal, you’ll be the linchpin that helps us scale and thrive responsibly, all while making a lasting positive impact.

If you worked here this past month here are some things you might have been involved in

Shaping our legal team's direction: You would have collaborated with our Head of Legal to define goals and priorities, ensuring our legal strategy aligns with the company's bigger picture.

Navigating new product launches: You might have been reviewing contracts and advising on compliance for exciting new product lines as we expand our reach.

Mentoring future legal stars: You could have been sharing your knowledge with a junior lawyer on secondment, helping them tackle a complex issue or providing guidance that supports their professional growth.

Making legal easy to understand: You'd have been translating complex legal jargon into clear, actionable advice for our marketing or operations teams, making sure everyone's on the same page.

Championing smarter ways of working: You might have been exploring and implementing new legal tech or processes to boost efficiency and make legal support even more accessible.

Skilful negotiations: You could have been in the thick of negotiations for a key partnership, securing outcomes that are beneficial for our mission and our business.

Staying ahead of the curve: You'd have been keeping a close eye on global legal changes, ensuring our advice is always accurate and we're prepared for what's next.

Let’s talk about you

You're more than just legally brilliant; you're a proactive leader with a knack for getting things done. You're someone who:

Minimum 5 years+ PAE: 10years+ PAE & in-house experience desirable

Thrives on strategy: You enjoy collaborating to set clear goals and work with the Head of Legal to develop effective plans for the team.

Influence: You understand the benefits of finding win win solutions, you develop strong relationships, and pro-actively engage with stakeholders to influence risk maturityIs a project management whiz: You can skillfully manage multiple legal projects, keeping stakeholders aligned and initiatives on track.

Leads with both directness and empathy: You're great at fostering collaboration, providing constructive feedback, and navigating challenging conversations respectfully.

Drives tangible results: You're focused on achieving measurable outcomes, always looking for ways to improve processes and deliver real value.

Communicates clearly and simply: You can break down complex legal information for non-legal audiences and champion user-friendly legal solutions.

Possesses strong negotiation skills: You have excellent technical legal skills and can confidently handle complex matters, achieving favourable outcomes while maintaining positive relationships.

Provides savvy commercial advice: You offer clear, pre-emptive legal advice that balances risk and commercial success, identifying both risks and opportunities for the business.

Is committed to continuous growth: You're always seeking ways to improve processes, stay updated on legal developments, and contribute to a culture of ongoing learning.

Enjoys mentoring others: You genuinely like guiding and supporting junior team members, and educating the broader business on all things legal.

You give a crap

Do you want your work to make the world a better place? Do you want to work with other people who feel the same way? What a coincidence — us too!

Why should you work with us?

First off, as a certified B Corp™, we work to make a difference every day while maintaining the highest standards of social and environmental impact. With our most recent score of 125.5 we’re in very good company with other exceptional B Corps around the world.

We also believe that helping to make the world a better place should be rewarded accordingly – that’s why we offer competitive, market informed salaries, meaningful support towards healthcare for our team around the world, generous paid leave, tailored learning and development opportunities, and free toilet paper (yes, you read that right).

Our engagement surveys (thanks Culture Amp!) tell us that our team is really proud (95%) to work for Who Gives A Crap and, well, we couldn’t be more proud of that.

Have you made it this far?

If you’re still reading, we think there’s a strong chance you might be our kind of person. Here’s the thing, though — research suggests that 60% of women and underrepresented folks might have already talked themselves out of applying. Even if you don’t check every box above, we want to encourage you to introduce yourself. We believe a diversity of perspectives and experiences makes a team stronger — and the stronger our team, the closer we are to delivering toilets and clean water for all.

Morning Brew’s newsletter, read by more than 4 million people seven days a week, offers a recap of the day’s news from the business world and beyond in just a five-minute read. Its secret sauce is not just expert curation of the news, but also the way that information is presented—in a friendly, funny, and inclusive voice. We deliver all the important updates our readers need to start their day without making them want to crawl back into bed.

Morning Brew has also become a major force on social channels such as Instagram, Twitter, and TikTok. On these platforms, the Brew brings the same blend of style and information to engage readers when they’re not in their inbox.

The purpose of this role is to maintain the continuity and quality of the Brew’s newsletter and social accounts from the end of the week through the weekend.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Write for the flagship newsletter, writing at least one story per day, as well as a weekly market recap and week ahead preview

Contribute story ideas and pitches for the newsletter

Write up tweets or Instagram posts when major news breaks

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

A minimum of three years writing in a newsroom or media environment, ideally covering business, markets, or world events

Excellent editorial judgment and attention to detail

Comfort working under tight deadlines

Ability to use humor in your writing (puns encouraged)

Fluency with online publishing tools and collaborative workflows

Familiarity with social platforms and the ability to distill news stories into X-length posts and find the perfect meme to match

COMPENSATION $75,000 - $80,000 *Final offers for this job will be made within the parameters of the salary range provided, commensurate with experience. Total offer package to include benefits highlighted under our perks section below.

Compensation

Additional Information

HOW WE TREAT EACH OTHER

Respectful Candor -- We believe that engaging in timely, constructive, and open discourse is an act of respect that makes for a more transparent and productive work environment.

Empathy -- We establish a strong partnership of trust with our co-workers and partners. We build human connections in order to understand each other.

Inclusivity -- Morning Brew Inc is deeply committed to fostering a transparently inclusive workplace environment, and people of color, women, people with disabilities, veterans, and LGBTQIA+ candidates are strongly encouraged to apply. 

HOW WE TREAT OUR WORK

Curiosity -- We learn every day through deliberate inquiry and exploration. We re-examine assumptions to be a better company, offer better products, and become better colleagues.

Accountability -- We celebrate our successes and own our failures. Taking responsibility for our actions allows us to learn from our experiences.

Bias Toward Action -- We know speed matters in business so we embrace quick and calculated risk-taking. We understand that many actions are reversible and therefore we are solutions-oriented, even when facing obstacles and challenges.

Challenger Mentality -- We don’t allow ourselves to be comfortable with our success. We are hungry to become the best and create more value for our audience.

Clarity of Purpose -- We understand the “why” in our work, which helps us to operate at our highest level of performance and efficiency.

PERKS

While being surrounded by a bunch of cool people who look great in crewnecks is its own reward, we have plenty more to offer. 

Brew’s HQ: Pick an adjustable standing desk or cozy corner and load up on free coffee (duh) and snacks at our new two-story office space in NYC’s Flatiron District.

401(k) employer match: We want to help you prepare for the future, now. 

Premium health, vision, and dental plans: Your health matters!

Mental health benefits: Personalized plans and programs to promote your mental well-being.

Extra help when you need it: Including a care concierge, plus free access to One Medical and the Calm app.

Family planning: Want to join #brewparents? Generous paid parental leave and fertility coverage for eligible employees.

Employee Resource Groups: Black Coffee, LGBTQ Brew, AAPI Brew, Cafe Con Leche, and Grounded

Gym and workout class reimbursements: It pays to be healthy.

Annual learning credit: Want to learn something new? We'll reimburse you.

BRIEF BREW HISTORY

Morning Brew Inc. was founded in 2015 by two entrepreneurial college students who noticed their peers were not consuming legacy media resources about business and finance news, but had a high desire to learn about those topics. What started as a small on-campus email has since evolved into a multi-channel media company that operates 20+ unique content franchises. All while maintaining our witty, honest and engaging tone that millions of loyal MBI audience members rely upon daily to better navigate the world. 

In 2020 a majority stake in MBI was acquired by Axel Springer SE and in February 2025 that position was increased to full ownership of the business. Axel Springer SE is a family-owned, transatlantic media company headquartered in Berlin and New York that is committed to the values of a free and informed society. To learn more about Axel Springer SE and what defines us, visit http://axelspringer.com/en/what-defines-us.

jobs.description:
Nash is looking for a Technical Support Specialist to join our global, 24/7 Technical Support team. This role sits at the heart of how Nash stabilizes the platform for our enterprise merchants - owning the investigation, resolution, and clean escalation of complex platform and integration issues across our delivery orchestration system.

Technical Support is Nash's intake and stabilization layer for everything beyond high-volume delivery inquiries. You'll be the person customers and internal teams rely on when something unusual is happening on the platform: a stuck integration, an unexpected provider behavior, a configuration question that needs real investigation. You'll resolve what you can, escalate what you can't with the context needed to move quickly, and help build the knowledge base that makes the next occurrence faster.

This is a role for someone who enjoys the detective work of complex, ambiguous technical problems, communicates clearly under pressure, and takes ownership seriously.

LOCATION

Remote in Australia (required)

AEST - Friday - Tuesday, 11A - 8P

TRAINING

4 weeks, Monday - Friday 

A note on location

This is a remote role, but candidates must be located in Australia. This is a hard requirement driven by contractual data access obligations with our enterprise customers, not a preference - we are not able to make exceptions.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Platform and integration investigation. Diagnose configuration questions, known error patterns, API and webhook issues, and account-specific behavior across the Nash platform.

Escalation quality. When an issue needs Engineering or Enterprise Operations, you own the handoff — clear reproduction steps, investigation performed, impact assessment, and severity. Escalations from this team are expected to be actionable on arrival.

Incident coordination. Serve as the active shift team for P1 incidents — coordinating communication, engaging Engineering immediately, and keeping customers and internal stakeholders informed through resolution.

Proactive monitoring. Watch Datadog dashboards, alerts, and logs for anomalies and emerging risks. Surface issues before they become customer-impacting where possible.

Knowledge base contribution. Document resolution patterns for novel issues so the next occurrence becomes a known pattern. Your work directly reduces future escalation volume.

Overflow support. Act as overflow for Delivery Support during peak windows when issues exceed their scope.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

5 - 6+ years in Technical Support, Support Engineering, or a related technical role in a SaaS environment

Hands-on experience investigating complex platform issues - not just routing tickets, but actually diagnosing what is happening

Comfort with APIs, webhooks, and integration troubleshooting in a production environment

Experience with monitoring and observability tools (Datadog, New Relic, Grafana, or similar)

Clear, calm written communication — especially during incidents or when customers are frustrated

Judgment about when to investigate further versus escalate, and the discipline to document thoroughly either way

Located in Australia (remote)

NICE TO HAVE

Experience supporting logistics, marketplace, or high-volume transactional platforms

Prior incident response or post-mortem participation

Experience contributing to knowledge bases or support documentation that actually gets used

Familiarity with ticketing platforms like Pylon, Zendesk, or similar

More about Nash

Nash is the platform that powers modern logistics.

Commerce has inverted. For decades, customers came to where products and services were. Now products and services come to them, on their terms, in real time. That shift has turned every company into a logistics company, even though almost none of them were built to be one. Couriers, fleets, gig workers, parcel carriers, in-store labor, and increasingly autonomous systems all have to be coordinated in real time, against tighter windows and rising expectations, with hard-fought customer trust on the line.

Nash unifies decisioning, execution, and capacity into a single programmable platform. Real-time, AI-native intelligence determines what should happen, operational control executes it, and the platform dynamically orchestrates capacity from any source: a company's own fleets, partners, or the Nash delivery network. Whether a job involves a courier, a gig driver, an internal fleet, a store employee, a technician, or an autonomous vehicle, Nash selects the right resource and manages execution through completion.

We power delivery and logistics for some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, 7-Eleven, and Woolworths, alongside platforms like Shopify and Toast. Over the next decade, logistics will become as foundational to commerce as payments, cloud, and connectivity. Nash is the platform that powers it.

Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman (2x Founder, MIT) and Aziz Alghunaim (2x Founder, 2x YC, Ex-Palantir, MIT) and is backed by Y Combinator, a16z, and other top investors. We are headquartered in San Francisco.

What You’ll Love About Us

✅ Early-stage, well-funded startup – directly impact the company and grow your career!
✅ Quarterly broader team on-sites to bond with teammates
✅ Competitive compensation and opportunity for equity
✅ Flexible paid time off
✅ Health, dental, and vision insurance for US employees

jobs.description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

The Opportunity 

Grafana Labs is looking for an Enterprise Account Executive, Acquisition based in Italy who will be responsible for prospecting and closing new business across Italy. You will identify, nurture and close opportunities with new customers, manage forecasts and track customer data. We're strong proponents of a consultative sales approach - learn about the customer's needs first before talking products. Your expertise will be critical in helping articulate the value of our products, work with the customer during the trial phase and hand off a strong relationship to our Growth team. Ideally, you come from a technical background and have sold technical products before.

What You’ll Be Doing

Meet and exceed individual quarterly and annual sales goals

Outbound prospecting into net-new customers

Manage all aspects of the sales process (prospecting, sales meetings, product demos, proofs of concept, proposals, and negotiations)

Cultivate sales through outbound prospecting and inbound leads

Be able to understand and convey the value of both Grafana Cloud and Grafana Enterprise

Become an expert in managing your sales pipeline in Salesforce

Manage quote creation, order processing, and day-to-day customer requests

What Makes You a Great Fit:

5+ Years of experience in infrastructure technology sales

Demonstrated history of consistent goal achievement in a highly competitive environment (top 10% performer)

Energetic, upbeat, entrepreneurial, tenacious team player

Adaptable and with demonstrable experience in high velocity technology companies

You will need to be an excellent communicator in all channels (in person, online, in writing) and able to form strong working relationships both in person and virtually

Fluent in English & Italian. 

 Bonus Points For: 

Familiarity with open source technology is a significant advantage

Experience using Salesforce

Experience using Command of the Message and MEDD(P)ICC is ideal

Compensation & Rewards 

In Italy, the OTE compensation range for this role is EUR 170,000 - EUR 211,250. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally. 

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.

Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.

Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.

Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.

Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.

Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.

Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.

Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.

Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.

In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it. 

Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.

Equal Opportunity Employer: Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. We believe that equality and diversity build a strong organisation, and we work hard to ensure that is the foundation of our organisation as we grow.

Grafana Labs may utilize AI tools in its recruitment process to assist in matching information provided in CVs to job postings. The recruitment team will continue to review inbound CVs manually to identify alignment with current openings.

Serve as the future operator of an integrated commercial function unifying pricing, deal desk, contract negotiation, and adjacent capabilities, governing price and discount on a ~$250M Enterprise ARR base

Co-manage future-state design of the function and end-to-end commercial process redesign.

Integrating today's fragmented pricing, deal desk, contracts, and RFP resources into one function.

Redesign commercial processes for speed and productivity with AI as a radical enabler.

Define enabling systems requirements across CPQ, approval workflows, and contract lifecycle.

Responsible for driving measurable ARR and productivity improvement through stronger pricing, discounting, and deal management by owning commercial policy, approval frameworks, and exceptions.

Lead with an AI-first mindset. Use data, automation, and tooling, including Claude, to optimize the commercial processes, monitor KPIs, and continuously raise the bar on performance.

Build and lead the function's team; partner and collaborate at the executive level with Sales, Legal, and Finance.

Process redesign expertise with an AI/automation-forward orientation

Executive presence and cross-functional authority across Sales, Legal, and Finance

Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs.
