Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

Grafana Labs is looking for a Enterprise Account Executive, Acquisition who will be responsible for prospecting and closing new business across the Florida region. You will identify, nurture and close opportunities with new customers, manage forecasts and track customer data. We're strong proponents of a consultative sales approach - learn about the customer's needs first before talking products. Your expertise will be critical in helping articulate the value of our products, work with the customer during the trial phase and hand off a strong relationship to our Growth team. Ideally, you come from a technical background and have sold technical products before.

Responsibilities

Meet and exceed individual quarterly and annual sales goals

Outbound prospecting into net-new customers

Manage all aspects of the sales process (prospecting, sales meetings, product demos, proofs of concept, proposals, and negotiations)

Cultivate sales through outbound prospecting and inbound leads

Be able to understand and convey the value of both Grafana Cloud and Grafana Enterprise

Become an expert in managing your sales pipeline in Salesforce

Manage quote creation, order processing, and day-to-day customer requests

Requirements

5+ Years of Experience in Infrastructure Technology Sales

Demonstrated history of consistent goal achievement in a highly competitive environment (top 10% performer)

Energetic, upbeat, entrepreneurial, tenacious team player

Adaptable and with demonstrable experience in high velocity technology companies

Familiarity with open source technology is a significant advantage

You will need to be an excellent communicator in all channels (in person, online, in writing) and able to form strong working relationships both in person and virtually

Bonus Points For:

Experience using Salesforce

Experience using Command of the Message and MEDD(P)ICC is ideal

REVENUE ACCOUNTANT 

Skillsoft is seeking a detail-oriented and analytical Revenue and Royalty Accountant to join our Revenue Accounting team. In this role, you will support the accurate recognition and reporting of revenue in accordance with U.S. GAAP and ASC 606, while also supporting accounting activities related to third-party royalty and reseller partners. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys working with financial data, interpreting contracts, proactively identify and implement process improvements, and partnering cross-functionally to drive efficiencies and strengthen controls. You will gain exposure to SaaS revenue recognition, deferred revenue, royalty accounting, month-end close, and revenue systems in a dynamic technology environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Support revenue recognition activities in accordance with ASC 606 and Skillsoft's accounting policies.

Review customer contracts, sales orders, amendments, and other agreements to identify key revenue accounting considerations.

Prepare and maintain revenue schedules for SaaS subscriptions, professional services, and other revenue streams.

Support monthly revenue roll-forwards and investigate variances between subledger, billing, and general ledger activity.

Manage and process royalty and reseller partner reports and payments in accordance with contractual terms.

Calculate royalty revenue, minimum fees, and other partner-related accounting amounts, as applicable.

Monitor royalty and reseller reporting requirements and follow up with internal and external partners for missing or incomplete information.

Maintain accurate documentation supporting revenue recognition and royalty accounting conclusions.

Partner with Sales Operations, Order Management, Legal, Accounts Receivable, Partner Management, and other teams to resolve contract and accounting discrepancies.

Assist with external and internal audit requests, including providing supporting schedules and documentation.

Support SOX controls related to revenue and royalty accounting and ensure assigned controls are completed accurately and timely.

Maintain accurate data and reporting within revenue, billing, and ERP systems.

Identify opportunities to improve revenue and royalty accounting processes, reporting, and controls.

Support special projects and system initiatives related to revenue recognition, royalty accounting, and process automation.

 

SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED:

2-4 years of accounting experience, which can include relevant internship or co-op experience with a Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

Knowledge and understanding of U.S. GAAP and accounting principles.

Strong Excel skills, including PivotTables, XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP, and common financial formulas.

Ability to review and interpret contracts, pricing terms, and financial data.

Robust analytical and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail.

Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet month-end deadlines.

Polished written and verbal communication skills.

Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams and communicate accounting requirements to non-accounting stakeholders.

Comfortable working with large data sets and identifying trends, variances, and discrepancies.

Ability to learn new accounting systems, processes, and technology quickly.

Demonstrated commitment to accuracy, accountability, and continuous improvement.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Experience with:

ASC 606 or revenue recognition.

Working in a SaaS, software, subscription, or technology company.

Royalty accounting, reseller accounting, licensing agreements, or partner reporting.

NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, or another ERP system.

Revenue recognition or billing systems.

Familiarity with deferred revenue and revenue reconciliation processes.

Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote position. We are considering candidates in Germany, Sweden, Spain, Ireland and the UK only.

The opportunity:

Grafana Cloud is our composable observability platform that integrates metrics, logs, traces, and profiles with Grafana. It allows our customers to leverage the best open source observability software – including Prometheus, Mimir, Loki, Tempo, and Pyroscope – without the overhead of installing, maintaining and scaling their own observability stack.

The Observability department is focused on enabling developers to understand the health and performance of their applications and infrastructure in any environment by providing tools to instrument their code, ingest observability data into Grafana Cloud and visualize and explore it.

What is the Ingest team?

We build and maintain the configuration and deployment tooling that bridges the gap between "I want observability" and "I have observability,". To achieve this the team owns Fleet Management, the Kubernetes Monitoring Helm Chart, and the Instrumentation Hub. Fleet Management is the cloud-based central control plane our customers use to manage hundreds of thousands of Observability Collectors in the wild. The Kubernetes Monitoring Helm Chart is used to effectively deploy Observability Collection in Kubernetes based environments. The Instrumentation Hub seamlessly combines Fleet Management and the Kubernetes Monitoring Helm Chart to achieve a magic 1-command instrumentation experience.

What You'll Be Doing:

Manage and develop the team of backend and frontend engineers, providing regular feedback and supporting each person’s growth through career conversations. This is a remote team, distributed between EMEA and NASA.

Collaborate closely with go-to-market to ensure customers and prospects are successful with their Observability collection journey.

Work closely with product and engineering leadership to ensure Fleet Management, the Kubernetes Helm Chart, and the Instrumentation Hub fit seamlessly into the end-to-end user experience for Grafana cloud products.

Provide guidance throughout the project lifecycle from early ideation through planning, execution and post‑launch guiding the team to deliver high‑quality results consistently.

Foster a psychologically safe environment where engineers can learn, experiment and iterate quickly, encouraging innovation and a culture of continuous improvement.

Work across team boundaries by contributing to projects outside your team’s scope and partnering with other functions to solve customer problems.

As a company we are remote-first and global, we embrace people of different experiences and backgrounds to build diverse teams where every person brings a new perspective to the software. 

We invest heavily in developer productivity. You can use modern AI coding assistants as part of your daily workflow (your choice of tools, within security guidelines), backed by a company-funded usage budget so you can iterate quickly without unnecessary friction. We encourage pragmatic AI-assisted development: faster prototyping, test generation, refactors, documentation, and incident follow-ups—always paired with strong code review and quality standards. You'll also have access to the latest frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

Experience in either of these areas is a strong advantage: Observability (especially OpenTelemetry), or building a central control plane that manages fleets of collectors.

You will be comfortable working with engineering teams who have a strong sense of autonomy in their decision-making, be it technical or product focused.

While you’re great with people and adept at managing relationships, you still keep up-to-date with the latest technical trends and shifts in order to maintain and enhance your understanding of the challenges your teams face.

Comfortable collaborating across time zones and cultures in a fully remote environment, using clear, empathetic communication to build trust, connection, and psychological safety.

Demonstrated ability to manage complexity, align stakeholders, and elevate team performance to deliver meaningful, high-quality results.

Deeply customer-focused, consistently grounding decisions and technical choices in user needs and real-world impact.

Solid understanding of distributed systems principles, including scalability, fault tolerance, consistency, and observability.

Comfort with AI-assisted tooling. We embrace AI and agentic development so we expect you to be curious and comfortable using AI-powered tools and ideally have practical experience folding them into a team’s workflow. 

Compensation & Rewards:

In the UK, the Base compensation range for this role is GBP 103,000 - GBP 129,000. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.

Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.

Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.

Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.

Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.

Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.

Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.

Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.

Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.

In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it. 

Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.

Equal Opportunity Employer: Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote position. We are considering candidates in Germany, Sweden, Spain, Ireland and the UK only.

The opportunity:

Grafana Cloud is our composable observability platform that integrates metrics, logs, traces, and profiles with Grafana. It allows our customers to leverage the best open source observability software – including Prometheus, Mimir, Loki, Tempo, and Pyroscope – without the overhead of installing, maintaining and scaling their own observability stack.

The Observability department is focused on enabling developers to understand the health and performance of their applications and infrastructure in any environment by providing tools to instrument their code, ingest observability data into Grafana Cloud and visualize and explore it.

What is the Ingest team?

We build and maintain the configuration and deployment tooling that bridges the gap between "I want observability" and "I have observability,". To achieve this the team owns Fleet Management, the Kubernetes Monitoring Helm Chart, and the Instrumentation Hub. Fleet Management is the cloud-based central control plane our customers use to manage hundreds of thousands of Observability Collectors in the wild. The Kubernetes Monitoring Helm Chart is used to effectively deploy Observability Collection in Kubernetes based environments. The Instrumentation Hub seamlessly combines Fleet Management and the Kubernetes Monitoring Helm Chart to achieve a magic 1-command instrumentation experience.

What You'll Be Doing:

Manage and develop the team of backend and frontend engineers, providing regular feedback and supporting each person’s growth through career conversations. This is a remote team, distributed between EMEA and NASA.

Collaborate closely with go-to-market to ensure customers and prospects are successful with their Observability collection journey.

Work closely with product and engineering leadership to ensure Fleet Management, the Kubernetes Helm Chart, and the Instrumentation Hub fit seamlessly into the end-to-end user experience for Grafana cloud products.

Provide guidance throughout the project lifecycle from early ideation through planning, execution and post‑launch guiding the team to deliver high‑quality results consistently.

Foster a psychologically safe environment where engineers can learn, experiment and iterate quickly, encouraging innovation and a culture of continuous improvement.

Work across team boundaries by contributing to projects outside your team’s scope and partnering with other functions to solve customer problems.

As a company we are remote-first and global, we embrace people of different experiences and backgrounds to build diverse teams where every person brings a new perspective to the software. 

We invest heavily in developer productivity. You can use modern AI coding assistants as part of your daily workflow (your choice of tools, within security guidelines), backed by a company-funded usage budget so you can iterate quickly without unnecessary friction. We encourage pragmatic AI-assisted development: faster prototyping, test generation, refactors, documentation, and incident follow-ups—always paired with strong code review and quality standards. You'll also have access to the latest frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

Experience in either of these areas is a strong advantage: Observability (especially OpenTelemetry), or building a central control plane that manages fleets of collectors.

You will be comfortable working with engineering teams who have a strong sense of autonomy in their decision-making, be it technical or product focused.

While you’re great with people and adept at managing relationships, you still keep up-to-date with the latest technical trends and shifts in order to maintain and enhance your understanding of the challenges your teams face.

Comfortable collaborating across time zones and cultures in a fully remote environment, using clear, empathetic communication to build trust, connection, and psychological safety.

Demonstrated ability to manage complexity, align stakeholders, and elevate team performance to deliver meaningful, high-quality results.

Deeply customer-focused, consistently grounding decisions and technical choices in user needs and real-world impact.

Solid understanding of distributed systems principles, including scalability, fault tolerance, consistency, and observability.

Comfort with AI-assisted tooling. We embrace AI and agentic development so we expect you to be curious and comfortable using AI-powered tools and ideally have practical experience folding them into a team’s workflow. 

Compensation & Rewards:

In Sweden, the Base compensation range for this role is SEK 878,000 - SEK 1,098,000. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.

Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.

Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.

Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.

Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.

Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.

Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.

Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.

Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.

In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it. 

Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.

Equal Opportunity Employer: Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. As part of the team, your skills will help organizations understand what skills they have, what they need next, and how to apply them in ways that drive real performance and progress.

Equity Plan Administrator

Skillsoft is seeking an experienced Equity Plan Administrator to be responsible for the accurate, timely and compliant administration of Skillsoft’s global equity programs and related public-company reporting activities. In this role, you will have the opportunity to partner closely with Legal, Human Resources, Payroll, Tax and Finance, supports employees and executives, and serves as a key operational owner for equity systems, controls, filings and vendor relationships.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Administer Skillsoft’s equity plans and awards, including RSUs, PSUs, stock options and other awards, from grant setup and participant communication through acceptance, vesting, release, exercise, forfeiture and termination processing.

Maintain complete and accurate participant, award, tax, share-pool and plan data in Equity Edge Online and related systems; monitor Workday integrations, resolve exceptions and reconcile equity activity to supporting approvals and records.

Coordinate vesting and release events, including validation of market value, tax methods and withholding, payroll reporting, transfer-agent instructions, share issuance and post-event reconciliations.

Prepare and coordinate public-company equity and ownership compliance activities, including Forms 3 and 4, Section 16 tracking, EDGAR Next administration, S-8 share tracking and equity-related proxy calculations and support.

Execute and document equity-related SOX controls; prepare audit support, periodic reconciliations and monthly, quarterly and annual reporting for Accounting, Tax, Payroll, Legal and Human Resources.

Partner with Legal and Human Resources on award approvals, grant agreements, insider-trading administration, blackout and trading-window communications, preclearance requests, stock ownership guideline tracking and required employee communications.

Prepare and coordinate international equity reporting and filings with local payroll teams and external advisors; support accurate tax withholding and reporting across jurisdictions.

Own day-to-day relationships with the equity platform provider, transfer agent, filing provider and other external advisors; respond promptly and professionally to participant questions and develop training and reference materials.

Monitor regulatory and market-practice developments affecting equity administration and recommend process, control and system improvements. Participate in other SEC reporting, governance or special projects as assigned.

REQUIRED SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS

8+ years of stock plan administration experience, preferably supporting global equity plans at a U.S. public company with a Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Human Resources or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

Hands-on experience with an equity administration platform such as Equity Edge Online; exposure to Workday, EDGAR Next, Section 16 filing software and transfer-agent processes is strongly preferred.

Advanced Excel and data reconciliation skills, with the ability to manage detailed records, complex calculations and competing deadlines with a high degree of accuracy.

Working knowledge of equity compensation, payroll and tax coordination, Section 16 reporting, securities-law compliance and SOX control requirements.

Excellent judgment, discretion, customer service and written and verbal communication skills; self-directed, highly organized and effective in collaborating across Legal, Human Resources, Payroll, Tax, Finance and external service providers.

Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

The Opportunity 

Grafana's Demand Generation team creates and accelerates pipeline across the full customer journey. We run a modern, AI-forward operation: lifecycle email programs driven by an AI engine, territory-level buying signals surfaced directly to sales leaders, and agentic workflows that handle work that used to take teams of specialists.

Our webinar program is one of the highest-leverage things we run: technical, practitioner-first sessions on a weekly cadence across AMER, EMEA, APAC and LATAM, putting the product in front of the people who would actually use it. Hands-on sessions, not sales pitches.

We're hiring a Webinar Program Manager to own it. This is a specialist seat, not a generalist one. You'll inherit an established program with a documented process and a full handover from the person who built it, and you'll own the operating rhythm from there: the calendar, the presenters, the build and promotion of every session, the follow-up, and the reporting.

This is not a "run the playbook" role. Sessions run in parallel at a pace no one could manage by hand, so the way to raise quality is to keep automating the mechanics. We expect this person to build with AI as a default and treat automation as a first-class deliverable, not a side project.

You'd be joining a demand gen team that is genuinely rebuilding how the function works, where AI agents run real production programs and the people on the team design the machine rather than turn the crank. The webinar program already produces, and much of the pipeline it touches starts with a session rather than a seller. You're not here to prove webinars matter. You're here to make each one produce more with less manual work behind it.

What You'll Be Doing

Own the webinar calendar end to end. Presenter booking, registration pages, campaign setup, promotion, live delivery, follow-up, and the flip to on-demand, across multiple regions and time zones.

Keep sessions practitioner-first. Brief technical presenters, shape the outline, and keep a session useful to the audience that registered for it.

Bring data to topic planning. Use past performance and downstream pipeline quality to recommend what we run and what we retire, and lock the plan with demand gen and product marketing each quarter.

Automate the production line. Extend the automation behind session setup and promotion, and keep pushing into the parts of the process a person shouldn't be doing by hand, including repurposing recordings into other content.

Report on what happens after the session. Registrations are the input. Connect sessions to product adoption and pipeline, report it honestly, and flag what isn't producing.

Grow the program's reach. Expand into additional languages and formats where the numbers justify it.

What Makes You a Great Fit

4+ years in demand generation, event marketing, or lifecycle marketing at a B2B software company (open source or developer-focused a plus).

Hands-on ownership of a recurring webinar or virtual event calendar across multiple regions. A cadence you were accountable for hitting, not a handful of one-off sessions.

Hands-on with a webinar platform (ON24, Zoom Webinars, Contrast, Goldcast or similar) and the plumbing behind it: CRM campaigns, registration sync, attendance data, follow-up triggers.

Comfortable working with technical presenters. You can brief an engineer or solutions architect and hold the line on what the audience came for.

Hands-on with AI in your actual work: you've built automations or agentic workflows (or are visibly on that path), and you think about AI as leverage, not a threat or a buzzword.

Comfortable with data: you can pull your own numbers, sanity-check them, and build a program readout a VP would trust.

Strong program management fundamentals. Twenty-plus moving pieces at once is a logistics job before it's a marketing job, and you ship on time without needing a coordinator.

Bonus Points For

Content repurposing at scale: clips, blog, social, on-demand libraries.

Localized program experience, and a view on when translation earns its cost.

Familiarity with the observability, monitoring or open source ecosystem.

Customer.io, Salesforce and a modern data stack (BigQuery or similar).

Experience with product-led motions alongside sales-led ones.

jobs.description:
About Us:

Spreedly is the Intelligent Payments Platform for businesses that want to own their payments strategy. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Durham, NC, we give merchants, platforms, and fintechs a single API to connect to 150+ payment gateways and 40+ payment methods across 100+ countries, along with the intelligence to decide where every transaction should go. We're vendor-agnostic by design. Our customers choose their providers, keep their payment data portable, and never have to rebuild their stack to adopt something new.

Payments are getting more complex, not less. Every new market, payment method, fraud tool, and now every AI agent checking out on a shopper's behalf adds another integration and another decision. Spreedly turns that complexity into an advantage. Our PCI Level 1 vault keeps cards and network tokens portable across providers. Smart routing and retries recover revenue lost to avoidable declines. Fraud and 3DS tools plug in with a single API call. And our payments intelligence turns transaction data into decisions merchants can act on. As agentic commerce moves from experiment to real sales channel, we're building the infrastructure that lets merchants accept agent-initiated payments through the providers they already trust.

For the people who work here, that means hard technical problems at real scale, billions of dollars in annual transactions, at a moment when the rules of commerce are being rewritten. If you want ownership and work that shows up directly in your customers' revenue, you'll fit right in.

About the Role

Spreedly is looking for a Support Engineer to take on our most complex customer issues and bridge the gap between support and engineering. You'll go beyond identifying a bug: you'll investigate where it occurs, explain its impact, and give engineering the evidence and technical context needed to resolve it.

You'll join an international support team that serves customers, partners, prospects, and internal colleagues. Our Tier 1 team provides round-the-clock support, while Tier 2 handles deeper technical investigations. This role brings additional engineering depth to that work, particularly in troubleshooting SDKs and complex payments integrations.

This is a hands-on, player-coach role. You'll work directly on difficult cases while helping teammates develop their technical skills. We also want this hire to help lay the foundation for a potential Tier 3 support function. That expansion and any future team leadership role are subject to leadership approval, rather than guaranteed next steps.

We expect roughly 60% of your time to focus on complex customer tickets, most of them from our top-tier accounts. The remaining time will involve retrospectives, customer advocacy, cross-functional projects, and coaching.

Responsibilities

Own complex technical investigations, particularly for our top-tier customer accounts. Read and navigate source code, analyze logs, and inspect API and SDK behavior to pinpoint issues.

Reproduce customer issues in test environments so findings are confirmed before they reach engineering.

Build clear, actionable engineering escalations that explain the problem, where it occurs, and potential approaches to resolving it, with engineering retaining final decisions on changes.

Bring SDK troubleshooting expertise to support for our Checkout SDK and share that knowledge across the team in collaboration with engineering.

Help manage incidents and keep customers informed, translating technical findings into clear explanations and advocating for their needs across departments.

Identify recurring patterns across cases, lead retrospectives, and turn findings into improvements that prevent repeat issues and reduce prolonged back-and-forth with engineering.

Improve documentation, share investigation techniques, and coach support teammates through unfamiliar technical problems.

Take ownership of cross-functional projects, from defining the problem through completing and rolling out the work.

 

Candidate Requirements

A foundation in software development through professional experience, coding education, or another hands-on path, with the ability to investigate code and explain technical findings.

Experience troubleshooting SDKs and working with APIs, including understanding how integrations behave in a web environment.

Customer-facing technical experience and the ability to communicate clearly with customers during complex or prolonged investigations.

The ability to coach others and lead work without formal authority. You don't need a previous management title, but you should be able to guide teammates and collaborate effectively with engineering.

Independent problem-solving and project ownership: you can work through ambiguity, move an investigation forward, and know when to bring others in.

Payments experience is strongly preferred because it will help you ramp quickly into complex customer cases. We're also open to candidates who can demonstrate the technical depth and learning ability to succeed without a payments background.

 

Additional Skills We Value

Familiarity with Ruby on Rails and SDKs across React, Android, or iOS.

Creating support processes, technical content, or tooling, including practical applications of AI in support.

Experience with Zendesk, Jira, or similar ticketing systems.

Spanish-language proficiency

We Offer Our US-Based Employees:

Competitive salary + Equity

Outstanding Medical and Dental benefits, including 100% employer-paid option

Company-paid Life and Disability insurance

Optional vision and supplemental insurance options, and various Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)

Open Paid Time Off policy + 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents

Matching 401(k) plan (5% up to $5,000 yearly)

$1,000 annual professional development stipend

Monthly home working/digital lifestyle stipend, new MacBook, and one-time accessory reimbursement

Access to company-paid professional coaching service

Visits to HQ in Durham, North Carolina for remote employee

Compensation

Additional Information

Spreedly Product Offering:

Spreedly provides an open payments platform. The platform’s connectivity provides payments performance. Key products and services include:

Connect — A unified API that integrates with hundreds of payment gateways, processors, and alternative payment methods worldwide, including digital wallets. Merchants access the global payments ecosystem through one connection.
Vault — A PCI-compliant secure repository for payment methods. Merchants store card data once and reuse it across any payment service, reducing PCI scope and protecting cardholder data at scale.
Optimize — Workflow-driven routing and retry logic that directs each transaction to the best-performing gateway in real time. On average, 7.9% of failed transactions succeed immediately when retried on a secondary gateway. This is where merchants recover lost revenue and increase authorization success rates.
Protect — A flexible fraud and authentication layer, incorporating advanced fraud tools and 3DS. Following Spreedly's acquisition of Dodgeball in September 2025, fraud orchestration and payment optimization now operate within the same platform.
Resolve — Centralized management and reporting that reduces operational silos, strengthens security, and improves billing control across a merchant's entire payment operation.
More Coming Soon! - Keep your eyes peeled for a new product launch by EOY '26

--

What It's Like to Work Here:

We describe our team as "Spreedlings": diverse, forward-thinking, and driven by a shared belief that a more open payments ecosystem benefits everyone. The company operates with a culture built on transparency, courageous collaboration, and self-driven leadership. The team values simplicity in both product and process, and approaches problem-solving with genuine curiosity.

--

We champion the ethical, creative use of AI—if you’re someone who pairs human judgment with modern AI tools to work smarter and drive bigger impact, you’ll thrive here.

--

Spreedly is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering, cultivating, and preserving a culture of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. We actively work to drive out even unintentional discrimination in our hiring processes via practices like blindly graded work samples, structured interviews, and diversity awareness training.

Due to the sensitive nature of what Spreedly does - handling payment data - finalist candidates must complete a successful background and reference check. 

At this time Spreedly is unable to provide sponsorship for employment, and we are not set up to support remote employees who reside in New York. In order to be considered for employment, applicants must be currently legally authorized to work in the job location country and not require future sponsorship in order to continue working in that country.

We appreciate your interest in our company. Because of the high volume of resume flow, we may only respond to those candidates that we think will be a potential fit.

--

jobs.description:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

Deepgram is looking for a Data Scientist to sit at the intersection between research and data: people who think deeply about what conversational data is actually composed of, what makes data valuable, and how to best leverage that.

Conversational audio presents incredibly rich scientific, engineering, and infrastructure challenges that are orders of magnitude harder than working with text. Speech carries speakers, accents, dialects, emotion, overlapping talk, code-switching, domain vocabulary, and acoustic conditions that range from a quiet studio to a drive-through — all with rich context that moves the conversation. In this role you'll collaborate closely with our research, engineering, and data teams to answer those questions rigorously and at scale. You'll care deeply about what makes conversational data difficult, you'll characterize it, and you'll shape the strategies that turn it into model gains. This role rewards conviction, creativity in approach, and a real appetite for overturning your own assumptions when the data says otherwise.

This is a hands-on, high-leverage role with unusual latitude to define an area from first principles. It reports to the VP of Data Operations. We're looking for people who:

See "we've always done it this way" as a starting position to argue with, not a constraint to work around

Can find the one experiment that settles a question in days rather than months

Are creative about where signal hides — in metadata, in model confidence, in the failures

Have the vision to take a scrappy proof-of-concept and scale it 100x

Are obsessed with using AI to automate and amplify their own impact

What You'll Own

Understand and characterize our data. Build the analysis that tells us what we actually have — languages, conditions, domains, speakers, quality — and what's underrepresented.

Design and build active-learning loops. Decide what's worth working on next based on where it will move performance, and make that decision systematic rather than intuitive.

Think deeply about how to best leverage humans in the loop. Human attention is the scarcest input in this system. Design the workflows, tooling, and model-assisted steps that make it count.

Make representative benchmarking possible. Build the curated datasets and methodology that let us make honest claims about model quality across the full diversity of real-world speech.Senior

Change our minds about what data strategies actually work. Run the experiments that separate what works from what everyone assumes works.

Care about data consistency, cleanliness, and organization — and about making data legible and accessible to non-technical teams, not just to the people who built the pipelines.

Bring method and automation to model adaptation. Turn one-off, domain- and customer-specific model work into repeatable, documented pipelines.

What We're Looking For

Hands-on work on real data pipelines and model-facing problems in data science, ML, or applied research

Strong Python and data tooling; comfort building analysis, scoring, and automation yourself

Experience with data characterization, data selection, active learning, or similar "what should we work on next" problems

Working familiarity with speech/audio or NLP models — you can reason about model output quality, confidence, and error modes

A track record of turning ambiguous, messy data situations into measurable model or product improvements

You build systems others run without you in the room — a reusable harness, not a one-off notebook

Strong communication skills, especially translating complex findings for audiences who don't share your background

An active AI-tool user. Not aspirational — tell us what you use and what you've built with it

It would be great if you also had:

Direct experience with ASR/TTS, audio data, or multilingual/code-switched data.

Experience with ensemble labeling, pseudo-labeling, or LLM-assisted annotation.

Familiarity with data provenance, PII/GDPR-aware pipelines, or model-improvement compliance.

Experience building custom or fine-tuned models for specific customers or domains.

jobs.description:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

Note: This individual must be based in either Eastern or Pacific Time in the US. or willing to work during these time zone work hours

Opportunity
Deepgram is seeking a talented, support-focused Solutions Architect (Applied Engineer) to join our Applied Engineering (AppEng) team. In this role, you will directly engage with customers to solve complex technical challenges while simultaneously building scalable solutions that enhance our support infrastructure. You'll own complete customer engagements in a post-sales capacity, and occasionally assist with pre-sales and implementation projects as needed. Your strong engineering background will enable you to resolve sophisticated technical issues, create repeatable solutions, and develop automation that allows the broader AppEng team to focus on high-impact pre-sales activities. This position offers an excellent path to grow into broader implementation and pre-sales roles while making an immediate impact on our customer support experience. As a key member of the Applied Engineering team, you'll influence our customer support strategy, and play a crucial role in ensuring our customers receive exceptional technical assistance throughout their journey with Deepgram.

About Applied Engineering at Deepgram
The Applied Engineering (AppEng) team at Deepgram combines the functions that other companies might separate into Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, Implementation, and Technical Support. We serve as the technical interface between Deepgram and our customers throughout their entire journey, from initial discovery and proof-of-concept, through implementation and onboarding, to ongoing technical support. We work closely with our Customer Success and Developer Experience (DX) teams to ensure a positive, growth-focused experience for our customers. This unified approach allows us to provide comprehensive technical guidance and build deeper relationships with our customers. As a support-focused Applied Engineer, you'll be primarily concerned with elevating our technical support capabilities while having opportunities to contribute to the broader Applied Engineering mission in pre-sales, implementation, and more.

What you'll do

Own the technical design and delivery of customer implementations and migrations, from kickoff through production cutover

Lead deployment scaling work, including capacity planning, rollout sequencing, and verification methodology

Design solutions that fit each customer's existing stack, constraints, and operational shape

Partner with Customer Success and Account Executives on customer-side change management, including readiness, stakeholder alignment, and rollout communication

Develop reusable implementation patterns, reference architectures, and deployment playbooks that the broader AppEng team and customers can reuse

Create automation and self-service tooling that compresses time-to-value for repeatable implementation work

Collaborate with product and engineering teams to advocate for customer needs and influence the roadmap based on patterns observed in active deployments

Provide support for the most complex post-onboarding cases when escalation crosses into Solutions Architect territory

Occasionally support pre-sales technical work, including discovery, scoping, and proof-of-concept design

Time allocation

50% — Customer implementation and scaling engagements

20% — Building reusable patterns, reference architectures, and automation

15% — Pre-sales technical support, including discovery, demos, and proof-of-concepts

10% — Documentation and knowledge sharing

5% — Complex post-onboarding escalations and collaboration with Technical Support Engineers

Your first 90 days

First 30 days — Complete comprehensive onboarding to understand Deepgram's technology, products, and the patterns we use for implementations. Gain proficiency with our core APIs and documentation. Shadow active implementation engagements to build familiarity with how the AppEng team operates during customer change phases.

60 days — Begin owning customer implementation engagements end-to-end, leading technical design and partnering with Customer Success on rollout. Start contributing to reusable implementation patterns and reference architectures.

90 days — Own the technical delivery of multiple concurrent customer implementations. Develop and deliver scalable solutions for repeatable customer change patterns. Begin contributing to the Applied Engineering team's implementation methodology and mentoring newer team members.

You'll love this role if you...

Enjoy seeing customer technical environments transformed through careful implementation work

Are passionate about reducing the time it takes any customer to reach production value with Deepgram

Find satisfaction in designing patterns that scale beyond a single customer engagement

Have a talent for identifying recurring needs across customers and translating them into reusable artifacts

Are energized by deploying cutting-edge Voice AI in production environments with real customers

See implementation work as a strategic function that drives customer growth and retention

It's important to us that you have

3+ years of experience implementing or deploying technical solutions for enterprise customers, ideally in customer-facing technical roles

Strong software engineering background with professional development experience in at least one modern programming language, such as Python, JavaScript / TypeScript, Rust, C / C++, or similar languages

Experience leading technical delivery of production deployments, from design through cutover

Proven ability to scope complex technical work and sequence it for successful delivery

Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to engineering and business stakeholders alike

It would be great if you had

Experience with speech recognition, natural language processing, AI Voice agents, or related AI technologies

Knowledge of cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure) and containerization technologies like Docker and Kubernetes

Experience with API-first products and developer tools

Background in change-management or implementation methodology

Experience producing reference architectures, deployment playbooks, or implementation templates

jobs.description:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile. 

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $16B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 150+ people across 25+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance. 

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.

The Role

At most companies, Sales Engineers are the technical sidekicks to sellers. At RevenueCat, in many cases, Sales Engineers are the sellers - the first touch for most inbound conversations, the ones helping prospects understand whether RevenueCat is right for them, and the people guiding them from curiosity to implementation.

As a Senior Sales Engineer, you’ll combine deep RevenueCat product knowledge with a consultative mindset. You’ll understand app monetization models, subscription infrastructure, and the growth levers that drive success. You’ll build and demo real examples - like replicating a prospect’s paywall in our builder - while explaining how our SDKs, APIs, and integrations fit (or replace) what they already have. When larger, complex deals involve multiple stakeholders or extended commercial negotiations, you’ll partner with a Strategic Account Manager, but for most, you’ll own the full technical and commercial conversation.

If you love combining technical depth, customer empathy, and a bit of marketing insight to help developers and app teams ship faster and smarter, this role is for you.

What You Will Be Responsible For

Technical Discovery and Solutioning

You’ll lead discovery calls and demos that bridge technical and business needs, exploring how RevenueCat’s SDKs, APIs, and growth tools integrate with existing systems. You’ll diagnose current setups, identify opportunities to simplify or improve, and occasionally build light proof-of-concepts - such as replicating a prospect’s paywall - to make the vision concrete. The goal is to help prospects make an informed decision, not to push a contract.

Customer-Centric Guidance

You’ll manage inbound conversations from first touch through technical validation, ensuring prospects get fast, honest, and actionable advice. You’ll balance what’s possible with what’s right, steering prospects toward the best path - whether that means a quick implementation, a longer evaluation, or sometimes deciding RevenueCat isn’t the right fit yet.

Scaling Evaluation Enablement

You’ll collaborate with developer and growth advocates to turn recurring questions into scalable content: short videos, walkthroughs, and sample apps that help thousands of developers self-evaluate RevenueCat. Eventually, you’ll maintain demo environments and internal resources that make it easier for the broader Sales, Success, and Support teams to work confidently with prospects.

Collaboration and Feedback Loops

You’ll act as the bridge between customers and our internal teams - sharing product feedback, surfacing common technical hurdles, and helping shape new features. As we’re gearing up to launch more standalone product experiences, this part of the role is absolutely critical: We’ll need your input to make sure that we’re building things that prospects actually need. You’ll work with Product Marketing and Growth to produce solution guides and launch materials that reduce friction in evaluations and accelerate time to first value.

Impact and Continuous Improvement

You’ll track and analyze the evaluation funnel: how fast prospects reach a decision, what slows them down, and how your involvement moves the needle. Your success isn’t measured in contracts signed, but in time-to-value reduced and new customers confidently shipping RevenueCat in production.

What Success Looks Like

Within 1 Month

You’ve ramped up on RevenueCat SDKs, APIs, and common integration patterns. After shadowing discovery calls, you deliver your first solo demo and contribute a small improvement, such as a new sample paywall or internal guide.

Within 3 Months

You’re managing the technical side of inbound deals end-to-end. You’ve launched your first one-to-many enablement asset and built a repeatable outreach or follow-up workflow that’s driving engagement. You confidently join forces with a Strategic Account Manager to help some of the world’s biggest apps evaluate RevenueCat.

Within 6 Months

Evaluation cycles in your pipeline are consistently shorter. You have published or updated at least two sample apps or integration guides and co‑hosted our bi-weekly office hours livestream or a public webinar with Marketing. You thoroughly understand the RevenueCat platform.

After 12 Months

You are the go‑to technical resource for complex, high‑value prospects. Conversion from form fill to win has increased in the segments you have owned. You mentor new Sales Engineers and contribute to scaling our enablement library.

What You Will Need to Be Successful

5 or more years in a customer-facing technical role such as sales engineering, solutions architecture, or developer advocacy for a SaaS or developer-tool company

Fluency with mobile stacks and comfort reading and writing Swift or Objective-C, Kotlin or Java, Flutter or Dart, or React Native with TypeScript

Strong communication skills that connect APIs and SDKs to business impact for both developers and non-technical stakeholders

Curiosity about how apps acquire, convert, and retain users and the ability to have an informed conversation about monetization

Organizational habits that keep multiple deals, demos, and content projects on track in a remote, async environment

A bias toward action: you’d rather ship a 70% solution today than a perfect one next quarter

Ideally, you also

Have shipped or integrated an app with RevenueCat

Have supported or closed enterprise SaaS deals and know how to navigate complex stakeholders

Understand subscription commerce, in-app purchases, or payments

Enjoy occasional whimsical side quests like creating a demo app that turns cat photos into subscription revenue

Are comfortable with tools such as Linear, Notion, Slack, Salesforce, and Looker

What we offer:

Competitive equity in a fast-growing, Series C startup backed by top-tier investors, including Y Combinator

10-year window to exercise vested equity options

A fully remote environment designed around autonomy and flexibility.

4-5 weeks of flexible time off annually

Paid desk at a co-working space

Workspace budget and continuous learning stipend

Interviewing at RevenueCat

Our interview process is rigorous on purpose. We want to be sure that everyone we bring on is genuinely excited about this work, aligned with how we operate, and ready to meet our high bar for performance. Curious what that actually looks like? Read more in our blog post on how we hire at RevenueCat, including tips to help you succeed.

More on how we work:

How we think about hiring and team design: Building a Winning Team

The values that guide how we work: Our Values

How we work as a remote team: How We Work Remotely at RevenueCat

What to expect from our interview process: Interview Expectations

What to expect from comp and employment: Employment FAQ

About Us:

Future is building a personalized guidance system for lifelong health. We help people understand what to do next for their body, goals, and stage of life — then support them in turning those decisions into sustained behavior change. By combining AI, human expertise, personal health data, and accountability, Future helps members improve performance today while building the resilience, capacity, and healthspan they need for decades to come.

Who We Are

Future pairs each member with an expert coach who gets to know them, their goals, and their data, then builds a healthier life around all of it. We started in fitness, and we're now going further: a coaching-led health experience that brings together movement, nutrition, sleep and recovery, and leverages real clinical data to build precise, custom member protocols. Our offering is continuing to evolve and we're looking for coaches who want to help shape it.

About the Role

Role Type: 1099 (independent contractor)

As a Health Coach, you'll own a caseload of members and guide each of them from their first day through their progress milestones. This is a partner role, not a prescriber role: you draw out what a member actually wants, meet them where they are, and help them build habits that last across nutrition, movement, sleep, and stress. You'll coach through a mix of virtual face-to-face sessions and day-to-day messaging, and you'll use each member's data to make your guidance specific and personal. The members we serve expect high-touch, polished care, with the coach at the center of their experience. 

What you'll do

Own your members' experience end to end. Guide a caseload of members from onboarding through their 90-day milestone and beyond, and keep every one of them feeling individually known.

Coach live and asynchronously. Run virtual kickoff and check-in sessions, and support members between sessions over messaging that stays warm, timely, and clear.

Build personalized, data-informed plans. With the support of AI tooling, translate each member's goals and data into a plan across fitness, nutrition, sleep, and recovery, and adjust it as their life and results change. 

Coach the person, not just the plan. Use motivational interviewing and reflective listening to help members find their own reasons for change and choose their own next step, rather than handing them a prescription.

Make the data useful. Under the guidance of Future’s Clinical Team, contextualize body composition scans, bloodwork and GLP-1 considerations within your scope, and turn them into everyday actions a member can take.

Make progress visible. Track progress against goals your members helped set, and celebrate the behavior and consistency wins, not just the number on a scan.

Help build. Bring what you learn from members back to the team, and help us shape a program that's ever growing and evolving. 

Who you are

Empathetic. You lead with care and meet people where they are, whether it's a member having a hard week or a teammate under pressure.

Independent, and collaborative. You can run your caseload at a high level without hand-holding, and you still genuinely enjoy working alongside your teammates.

An active part of the community. Even though we're a virtual company, you show up: you join calls, contribute to projects, and share honest feedback that makes the team better.

Proactive. You chase down answers, follow up, and take initiative instead of waiting to be told.

Tech-savvy. You pick up new tools quickly and are comfortable working across apps, data, and platforms all day.

What you'll need

Required (non-negotiable)

A health coaching certification from a recognized program covering behavior-change theory, motivational interviewing, reflective listening, and foundational nutrition, such as an NBHWC-approved program, ACE Health Coach, Precision Nutrition L1, NASM Behavior Change Specialist, or an equivalent. Full NBC-HWC board certification isn't required, but it's a strong preference.

An associate's degree or higher (or an equivalent, experience-based path to your coaching certification).

2+ years of client-facing coaching or training experience. Enough that you can run a member session on day one, without a ramp.

Proven high-volume caseload management. You've personally carried a large book of clients at once and kept each of them feeling individually known.

Comfort working with a diverse member population. You adapt your style to meet members of different ages, backgrounds, cultures, abilities, and health starting points, and every one of them feels respected and understood.

Strong written communication. Much of your coaching happens over messaging, so you're warm, clear, and personable on the page while staying professional.

Strong verbal communication and presence. You also coach face-to-face over video, and you bring confidence, thoughtfulness and professionalism into every session.

Comfortable synthesizing health data. You keep up with current health trends and have a track record of coaching clients across nutrition apps and wearable devices, bringing their data together into a single comprehensive plan.

Strong plus (not required)

A personal-training or strength credential (CSCS; NASM, ACE, or ACSM CPT; or similar).

A nutrition-coaching certification such as Precision Nutrition.

An advanced degree in exercise science, physiology, kinesiology, or a related field.

Clinical collaboration in functional or integrative medicine. You've worked alongside or under registered dietitians, nurse practitioners, or physicians.

Experience with luxury clientele. You've served high-end members in concierge medicine, a premium gym, or a private club, and you carry that polish into every interaction.

A distinct coaching specialty such as performance, postpartum, pelvic-floor, or eating-disorder-informed coaching, that adds range to our team.

Startup experience, or time spent in a fast-changing, still-being-built environment.

What we offer

Engagement Type

This is an 1099 independent contractor engagement, not employment. Contractors are engaged through a written services agreement, are responsible for their own taxes, and are not eligible for Future employee benefits.

Remote (residence in approved state) We are currently ONLY hiring in AZ, FL, GA, NC, OH, SC, TN, TX, UT.

Compensation

The compensation range for this engagement is $30–$40 per hour, based on experience and credentials.

Future is an equal opportunity organization. We consider qualified applicants without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable law. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered in accordance with applicable law, including the California Fair Chance Act.

 

Life at Future

Health Coverage: All employees who meet eligibility requirements receive comprehensive medical, dental, vision, and disability insurance, plus tax-advantaged savings accounts.

Wellness: Monthly wellness stipend for fitness, recovery, and overall wellbeing, plus access to mental health resources and therapy support.

Future Membership: Enjoy our platform for free.

You'll inherit a team of strong, motivated people and take on the work of further unifying them under a coherent educational strategy: one that serves customers directly through consulting engagements and Academy programs, and serves Ashby internally through how we train and enable our GTM teams to teach, demo, and demonstrate the value of Ashby.

About This Role
The goal of our Education team is to act as a CSM for every customer and GTM employee. We are principled in how we operate and create content and experiences that are truly useful to our audience. Our Academy consists of public-facing content and digital programs that aim to meet customers where they are — whether that's a Recruiting Manager just getting started with Ashby or a Head of Talent looking to improve Quality of Hire. Our RecOps Consulting team brings deep operational expertise to customers who need more than product guidance, through both 1:1 and scaled experiences. And our Product Enablement function exists to close the gap between what the product can do and what CS and sales teams can confidently apply in practice.

As Head of Education, you'll manage across all three of these functions and own the operating model that ties them together. At the start, this will mean being close to the work — managing ICs alongside early leaders and building out the leadership layer over time as the organization scales.

Day-to-day, this looks like:
RecOps Consulting
Overseeing RecOps Consulting, ensuring 1:1 customer engagements are driving real value, and that insights from direct consulting work find their way into Academy content rather than staying locked in individual engagements.

Partnering with Professional Services on scoping and delivering paid RecOps engagements — including how packages are structured, where the line sits between complimentary and paid work, and how the consulting model evolves by segment.

Academy
Partnering with the Manager of Academy on content strategy — what gets built, how it's organized, and how the library evolves as the product and customer base grow.

Building out new Academy programs, including a product certification path, centralizing the webinar function under CE, and launching a Digital Programs capability that brings education directly to customers through in-app and email experiences.

Product Enablement
Building out Product Enablement as a distinct function — translating the last 20% of product context for CSMs and AEs, addressing the continuous shipping problem for our field teams, and designing a new hire onboarding experience that's more durable than what we have today.

Team
Building the operating infrastructure that lets all three functions scale: intake processes, engagement frameworks, capacity planning, and the connective tissue that keeps the functions working together rather than in parallel.

While you'll start by managing a mix of Managers and ICs across Consulting and Academy, you’ll be responsible for identifying where additional layers are needed to effectively scale the org — either by developing from within or hiring externally.

Representing CE externally through webinars, industry events, and customer sessions — and synthesizing what you hear back into credible, specific product feedback.

There isn't one standard background that defines success in this role. If your experience includes building and scaling Recruiting Operations, Customer Success, or Customer Education functions, we'd encourage you to apply.

You Could Be a Great Fit If

You think from first principles about education. You're skeptical of "best practices" as a starting point and more interested in what actually serves the specific audience in front of you — whether that's a recruiter trying to figure out offer approvals or a CSM trying to explain a product release.

You're a strong leader of leaders. You develop the people beneath you deliberately, hold a high bar without micromanaging, and create an environment where your team does their best work.

You think in operating models. You can look at three distinct functions and figure out what they need to share, where they need to stay separate, and how to build systems without over-engineering.

You're energized by being close to the work. While you'll eventually have a leadership team in place, you'll start by directly managing our RecOps Consultants and Academy team.

You build strong cross-functional relationships. You'll need to partner closely with leadership counterparts across CS, Sales, Product, and Marketing — and the ability to show up as a credible, collaborative peer in those conversations is as important as what you build within CE.

You're comfortable with ambiguity and motivated by building. This is not a standard Education role and the team is still early — we need someone who can figure out how we scale and help build toward that.

You communicate with clarity and operate well in a writing-heavy culture. At Ashby, proposals, frameworks, and documentation are how decisions get made and work moves forward.

You think carefully about the full customer spectrum — from the team of one setting up their first ATS to the enterprise org navigating complex integrations — and can build programs that serve both without defaulting to just one end.

You're comfortable hopping into new tools and figuring them out. You won't necessarily be building, but you'll engage directly enough to support your team — whether that's understanding how an in-product journey gets configured or evaluating a new LMS feature.

You have a perspective on how consulting fits into an education strategy — where 1:1 expertise should scale into content, where it shouldn't, and how the two motions reinforce each other.

You Might Not Be a Great Fit If
You prefer to set strategy and hand it off. This role requires staying close enough to the work to build the systems and infrastructure that support it — not just directing others toward a vision and stepping back.

You're not comfortable in front of customers. There will be moments where you're supporting a RecOps Consulting engagement in a leadership capacity, or take the stage during an Ashby-hosted event.

You don't enjoy reviewing content. You'll be the final bar for what the team publishes and the experiences they create, and that means staying close enough to the work to know when something isn't ready.

You rely on industry playbooks to tell you what an education function should look like. We have strong opinions about what effective CE should be, and we're looking for someone who is principled and will build from first principles.

You find it hard to thrive when the scope is shifting. This function is constantly evolving as business needs shift, and you'll need to be genuinely energized by that rather than stabilized by a fixed remit.

Interview Process
Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes

Hiring Manager Interview with Global Head of Customer Success — 45 minutes

Presentation with CE team leads and cross-functional partners — 60 minutes

Final Panel:
VP of CS — 30 minutes

CEO Interview — 30 minutes

Closing Questions — 15 minutes

Benefits
Opportunity to work with a talented and passionate team.

10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby — do it when you feel financially comfortable.

Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it!

Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

$100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents with all premiums covered by us, and an automatic 401k match.

We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.
Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. BetterHelp is on a mission to remove the traditional barriers to therapy and make mental health care more accessible to everyone. Our network of over 30,000 licensed therapists has helped millions of people take ownership of their mental health and change their lives forever. And we’re not stopping there – as the unmet need for mental health services continues to grow, BetterHelp is committed to being part of the solution.

As the Head of Security at BetterHelp, you’ll join a diverse team of licensed clinicians, engineers, product pros, creatives, marketers, and business leaders who share a passion for expanding access to therapy. And as a mental health company, we take employee mental health just as seriously as we do our mission. We deeply invest in our team’s well-being and professional development, because we know that business and individual growth go hand-in-hand. At BetterHelp, you’ll carve your own path, make an immediate impact, and be challenged every day – with a supportive community behind you the whole way.

What are we looking for?

BetterHelp is seeking a highly technical Head of Security Engineering to lead our security strategy with a strong emphasis on offensive security and attacker mindset.

This role will anchor our security organization in a red team–first approach, proactively identifying vulnerabilities and strengthening our defenses before they can be exploited. In addition to leading offensive security, you will provide oversight and strategic direction across Security Operations (blue team) and Application Security, ensuring a cohesive and effective security posture.

Operate with a red team / attacker mindset, identifying vulnerabilities across applications, infrastructure, and internal systems

Direct and evolve the company’s red team capabilities, including penetration testing, code review, and vulnerability discovery

Provide oversight and guidance across:

Partner closely with Engineering to embed security into the software development lifecycle (SDLC)

Strengthen processes around vulnerability management, detection, and response

Build and improve offensive security tooling and capabilities, complementing external programs like Bugcrowd

Help reduce technical debt and improve system resilience through proactive security practices

Identify and address emerging threats, including AI security risks

Mentor and guide a strong team, setting a high bar for technical rigor and impact
